definition_zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名
definition_en: to put forward a plan or idea for others to consider; to ask someone to marry you; to intend to do something; to nominate someone formally
core_image: 一只手把写着想法的纸推到桌面中央，抬头看向众人
scene: 小组讨论卡住时，最年轻的成员把一张草稿推到桌子中间，请大家先看他的思路。She proposed a shorter timetable so that the team could test the design earlier.
sceneCN: 这里 propose 是「提出、提议」（第 1 个义项：把计划或想法提出来供人考虑）；句意为她提出一个更短的时间表，好让团队更早测试设计。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、圆桌、马克杯。

pos.zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名

derivatives.zh: propose 加名词后缀 -al（末尾 e 脱落），义为「提议；方案；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」
与 propose 同出拉丁 proponere，义为「命题；主张」
propose 的过去分词作形容词，义为「拟议中的；提议的」

senses.title: To put forward a plan or idea
senses.definition: to suggest a plan, idea, or course of action for other people to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出计划、想法或行动方案供他人考虑
senses.example: The engineer proposed a cheaper way to reinforce the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提出了一种更便宜的屋顶加固办法。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to place something in front of someone, so proposing is literally laying an idea on the table for others to look at.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「把东西摆到某人面前」，所以 propose 就是字面意义上的「把想法放到桌面上」让人看。

senses.title: To ask someone to marry you
senses.definition: to ask a person to marry you, usually in a formal or planned way
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人嫁给自己或娶自己，通常正式或经过安排
senses.example: He proposed to her beside the river where they first met.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两人初遇的河边向她求婚。
senses.why: An offer of marriage is placed before the other person like a plan, and the answer comes back as a decision in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 求婚也像一份方案那样摆到对方面前，对方的回答同样是一次决定。

senses.title: To intend or plan to do something (formal)
senses.definition: to intend to do something, especially as a stated plan
senses.definitionCN: 打算做某事，尤指作为已说明的计划
senses.example: The council proposes to close the lane to traffic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会打算在周日封闭这条小路，禁止车辆通行。
senses.why: What is set before people as a plan also states what the speaker means to do, so the verb comes to mark intention.
senses.whyCN: 摆在众人面前的计划同时也表明了说话人打算做什么，于是这个动词便能标示「意图」。

senses.title: To nominate someone or put a motion formally
senses.definition: to name a person for a position, or to present a motion for a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 提名某人担任某职，或提出动议交付正式表决
senses.example: She was proposed as the next chair of the society.
senses.exampleCN: 有人提名她担任协会的下一任主席。
senses.why: A name can be placed before a group just as an idea can, so one verb covers nominating a person and moving a motion.
senses.whyCN: 名字和想法一样都能被摆到一群人面前，所以同一个动词既能指提名某人，也能指提出动议。

intro.en: Propose comes from Latin pro- forward and ponere to place, through the French verb proposer; the same stem with the noun ending -al gives proposal.
intro.cn: propose 来自拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置），经法语动词 proposer 进入英语；同一个词干加上名词后缀 -al，就成了 proposal。

items.en: Ponere meant to place, set down, or fix in position, and it is the source of a large family of English words.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下、固定在某处」，是英语中一大族词的来源。

items.en: With pro- meaning forward, proponere meant to put forward or set before someone, often as an offer.
items.cn: 加上表示「向前」的 pro-，proponere 意为「向前摆出、呈现给某人」，常带「献上」的意味。

items.en: Old French proposer carried the sense of suggesting or setting out, and English took the verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 带有「建议、陈述」的意思，英语在十四世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: Modern English propose covers plans, intentions, marriage and nominations, while proposal names the thing offered.
items.cn: 现代英语的 propose 覆盖计划、意图、求婚与提名，而 proposal 指被献出的那个东西。

items.en: Propose ends in a silent e, which drops before the noun ending -al, so propos- plus -al becomes proposal, never proposeal.
items.cn: propose 以不发音的 e 结尾，遇到名词后缀 -al 时这个 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 写作 proposal，而不会写成 proposeal。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and the Latin relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting an idea or a name forward.
note.cn: 形近组收这个动词的名词形式与拉丁同族词；近义组收「提出想法或名字」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a plan or a marriage offer that is put forward.
entries.definitionCN: 由「提出」而来的名词，指方案或求婚。

entries.definition: A statement or idea offered for discussion or proof.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供讨论或证明的陈述、主张。

entries.definition: To put forward an idea or theory for serious consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重提出某种想法或理论供人考虑。

entries.definition: The aim of an action; only the spelling looks alike, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的目的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To mention an idea for someone to think about.
entries.definitionCN: 提出一个想法供人考虑。

entries.definition: To advise that something is a good choice.
entries.definitionCN: 建议某事物是好选择。

entries.definition: To formally name someone for a position.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提名某人担任某职。

entries.definition: To have something in mind as a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 心里打算做某事。

normalIntro.en: The verb is built from pro- forward and ponere to place, and its noun keeps the same stem with -al instead of a final e.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）构成，它的名词用同一词干加 -al，而不用末尾的 e。

normal.en: Propose is pro- forward plus ponere to place: to place an idea before people.
normal.cn: propose 是 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）：把想法摆到众人面前。

normal.en: Proposal is the same stem with -al, and the e of propose drops, so the noun is spelled propos-al.
normal.cn: proposal 是同一词干加 -al，propose 的 e 脱落，所以名词拼作 propos-al。

normal.en: Propose a toast and propose a plan use the same gesture of holding something out to others.
normal.cn: propose a toast 与 propose a plan 用的是同一个「把东西端给别人」的动作。

normal.en: Propose to someone keeps the offer image, with a shared life as the thing offered.
normal.cn: propose to someone 保留了「献上」的意象，只是献出的东西变成共同的生活。

normal.en: Propose a motion and propose a candidate both put a wording or a name in front of a group for a vote.
normal.cn: propose a motion 与 propose a candidate 都是把一段文字或一个名字摆到一群人面前等待表决。

abstract.en: The verb is an open hand: whatever it offers must be visible to the people who will decide.
abstract.cn: 这个动词就是一只摊开的手：它献出的东西必须让将要决定的人看得见。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a name all travel the same path, from a private thought to a public table.
abstract.cn: 计划、婚姻与名字走的是同一条路：从私下的念头，到公开的桌面上。

abstract.en: The missing e in proposal is the trace of the verb handing its meaning over to the noun.
abstract.cn: proposal 里少掉的那个 e，正是动词把意义交给名词时留下的痕迹。

examples.en: The city proposed a new bike lane along the river.
examples.cn: 市里提议沿河修一条新的自行车道。

examples.en: He proposed to her after dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭后，他向她求婚。

examples.en: They propose to move the office closer to the station.
examples.cn: 他们打算把办公室搬到离车站更近的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若剖子」——把想法剖开摆到桌上，就是 propose，提议。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）→ proponere（摆到前面）→ 古法语 proposer → 英语 propose；去 e 加 -al 即得 proposal，两者同源，词义都围绕「把东西摆到人前」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is setting something before people; the senses divide into a plan, an offer of marriage, a stated intention, and a formal nomination.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把东西摆到人前」；义项由此分为计划、婚姻的献出、已说明的意图，以及正式提名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a sheet of notes to the middle of the table and looking up at the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一张写满要点的纸推到桌子中央，抬头看向众人。

branches.en: a rough timetable pushed across a round table
branches.cn: 一张粗糙的时间表被推过圆桌

branches.en: a ring held out by the river at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时在河边递出的戒指

branches.en: a council paper stating what it means to do
branches.cn: 市政文件写明它打算做什么

branches.en: a name read aloud and seconded in a hall
branches.cn: 礼堂里念出一个名字并有人附议

branches.en: one verb for offering a plan and offering a life
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既献出方案，也献出一生

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb ponere, the prefix pro-, the French verb proposer, and the English nouns proposal and proposition.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词 ponere、前缀 pro-、法语动词 proposer，以及英语名词 proposal 与 proposition 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to put forward, to ask in marriage
a plan or offer put forward

definition_zh: 起诉；检控；（正式）继续从事、推行；追究到底
definition_en: to bring a criminal charge against someone and conduct the case
core_image: 一个人把一份文件按在桌上，沿着页边的编号一页页往下翻，翻到最后一页才停手
scene: 检方拿到新的银行记录之后，决定对那名会计正式提出指控。The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecute 指对某人正式提起刑事指控并推进案件（第 1 个义项：提起刑事起诉）；句意：新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。图中可辨识物件：银行记录、案卷页码、检察官办公桌、印章。

pos.zh: 起诉；检控（对某人提起并推进刑事指控）
提起公诉；进行起诉
（正式）继续从事、推行（某项工作、调查或事业）

collocations.zh: 进行战争（旧式正式说法）

derivatives.zh: 起诉；控方
检察官；公诉人
检察的；公诉的
可被起诉的

senses.title: Bring a criminal charge
senses.definition: to formally charge someone with an offence
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯罪
senses.example: The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind prosecution: what the office does when it decides a file should go to court.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 prosecution 背后的动作：当机构认定一份卷宗该送进法院时，它做的就是这件事。

senses.title: Conduct the case in court
senses.definition: to present and argue the state's case through the hearings
senses.definitionCN: 在庭审中陈述并论证国家的案件
senses.example: The office prosecuted the case for nearly two years.
senses.exampleCN: 该机关把这桩案子推进了近两年。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to follow forward, so the work is a long following of the case rather than a single filing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向前追随，所以这项工作是对案件的长程追随，而非一次立案。

senses.title: Press a civil claim
senses.definition: in legal writing, to pursue a claim or a suit to judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在法律文字中，把请求或诉讼追究至判决
senses.example: The creditor prosecuted the debt through two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人通过两级法院追究这笔债务。
senses.why: Before criminal law dominated the word, any claim could be prosecuted, and older legal writing still uses it that way.
senses.whyCN: 在刑法主导这个词之前，任何请求都可以被「追究」，较早的法律文字仍这样使用。

senses.title: Carry on an activity
senses.definition: in formal style, to continue or carry on a study, inquiry or policy
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，继续或推行一项研究、调查或政策
senses.example: The committee prosecuted its inquiry despite the delays.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管一再拖延，委员会仍把调查进行下去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is continuation, and formal prose keeps it alive for any sustained effort, not only for lawsuits.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「继续」，正式文字把它保留下来，用于任何持续的努力，而不限于诉讼。

senses.title: Pursue a war or campaign
senses.definition: in older usage, to carry a war or campaign forward energetically
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，有力地推进战争或战役
senses.example: The general prosecuted the campaign into the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 将军把战役推进到了冬季。
senses.why: Military writing used the verb for pressing an operation to its end, and that usage survives in histories and formal reports.
senses.whyCN: 军事文字用这个动词表示把一次行动压到终点，这一用法保存在史书与正式报告里。

senses.title: Carry out a duty or plan
senses.definition: in formal style, to carry out a duty, plan or design
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，执行一项职责、计划或设计
senses.example: She prosecuted the plan with a patience few colleagues shared.
senses.exampleCN: 她以少有人能及的耐心把这项计划执行下去。
senses.why: Any design can be followed through, and formal English uses the verb for that steady execution without any legal charge.
senses.whyCN: 任何设计都可以被贯彻到底，正式英语便用这个动词表示那种稳定的执行，与刑事指控无关。

senses.title: Follow up an appeal or remedy
senses.definition: to carry a legal remedy forward to the next stage
senses.definitionCN: 把一项法律救济推进到下一阶段
senses.example: They prosecuted the appeal all the way to the higher court.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把上诉一路推进到高等法院。
senses.why: A remedy has stages, and the verb marks the act of not letting the matter drop at the first refusal.
senses.whyCN: 救济是有阶段的，这个动词标记的正是「第一次被驳回也不放手」的那个动作。

senses.title: Pursue a goal relentlessly
senses.definition: in literary style, to pursue an aim with persistence
senses.definitionCN: 在文学文体中，坚持不懈地追求一个目标
senses.example: He prosecuted his ambition long after his friends had given up theirs.
senses.exampleCN: 朋友们早已放弃各自的抱负，他仍把自己的追求推进下去。
senses.why: The core image of following forward can describe any long pursuit, which is why the verb appears in writing about ambition.
senses.whyCN: 「向前追随」的核心意象可以描述任何长程追求，所以这个动词会出现在写抱负的文字里。

intro.en: Prosecute comes from the stem of Latin prosecutus, the past participle of prosequi 'to follow forward'. The verb was formed in English from that stem, and its oldest sense is continuation.
intro.cn: prosecute 来自拉丁 prosecutus 的词干，那是 prosequi「向前追随」的过去分词。这个动词是在英语中用该词干构成的，最古老的含义是「继续」。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it also stands behind sequence and consecutive, so the idea of one thing after another runs through the whole family.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，也是 sequence 与 consecutive 的来源，所以「一件接一件」的观念贯穿整族词。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, pursue, continue'. Roman legal writing used it for pursuing a charge.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。罗马法律文字用它表示追究一项指控。

items.en: The past participle prosecutus supplied the stem prosecut-, which English took as the base of both the verb and the nouns.
items.cn: 过去分词 prosecutus 提供词干 prosecut-，英语以它作为动词与名词的共同基础。

items.en: English formed prosecute from the participle stem, at first for continuing any business, then increasingly for the pursuit of a legal case.
items.cn: 英语用这个分词词干构成 prosecute，起初指继续任何事务，后来越来越多指追究一桩法律案件。

items.en: Legal writing fixed the criminal sense, pairing prosecute with indictment and trial, while the older sense of continuing survived in formal prose.
items.cn: 法律文字固定了刑事义，把 prosecute 与起诉、审判配对使用；而「继续」的旧义保存在正式散文中。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb mainly for criminal charges, with the sense of carrying out a duty, inquiry or war kept for formal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用这个动词指刑事指控；执行职责、进行调查或进行战争的义项则留给正式与历史文字。

note.en: Group one separates the related nouns from the classic hostile-prefix confusion and from a look-alike about looking forward; group two sets the verb against the other verbs of charging and suing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根名词、经典的「敌对前缀」混淆词，以及一个关于「向前看」的形近词；第二组把这个动词与其他表示指控和起诉的动词作对照。

entries.definition: To harass or oppress, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix replaces pursuit with mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指骚扰、压迫，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀把「追究」换成「迫害」。

entries.definition: The proceeding or the team; the verb names the act, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序或团队；动词命名的是动作，不是机构。

entries.definition: The lawyer who performs the act; the verb does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 执行这个动作的律师；动词本身不指人。

entries.definition: An outlook or a search for minerals, from prospicere 'to look forward'; it shares no following verb with prosecute.
entries.definitionCN: 指前景或找矿，来自 prospicere「向前看」；它与 prosecute 不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Capable of being prosecuted, a quality of a case rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被起诉的，是案件的性质，不是动作。

entries.definition: To charge formally, often after a grand jury; prosecute also covers the whole conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式起诉，常在大陪审团之后；prosecute 还覆盖案件的整个推进过程。

entries.definition: To state that someone has committed an offence; prosecute adds the decision and the conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指声明某人犯罪；prosecute 多了「决定起诉」与「推进案件」的意思。

entries.definition: To start a civil case; prosecute is the usual verb for criminal proceedings and can also mean carrying any claim forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起民事诉讼；prosecute 常用于刑事程序，也可指把任何请求推进下去。

entries.definition: To hear and decide a case in court; prosecute is the state's part before and during that hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法庭上审理并裁决；prosecute 是国家在庭审前后所做的那一部分。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for following an aim or a person; prosecute is its formal and legal doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 指追求目标或追踪某人的日常动词；prosecute 是它在正式与法律语境中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle stem and the real contrast between following a charge and harassing a person.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词词干，以及「追究指控」与「迫害他人」之间的真实对比。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: prosecuting a case means not letting it drop.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：起诉一桩案子就是不让它掉在地上。

normal.en: Persecute has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': it follows a person to hurt, not to court.
normal.cn: persecute 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀是「贯穿」：它跟住一个人是为了伤害，不是为了上法院。

normal.en: Prospect is about looking forward, not following: a different verb entirely.
normal.cn: prospect 讲的是向前看，不是跟随：完全另一个动词。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

normal.en: The old sense still works: a committee can prosecute an inquiry without charging anyone.
normal.cn: 旧义仍然可用：委员会可以把一项调查进行下去，而不指控任何人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger walking down a numbered page, page after page, until the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着编号的页面往下走，一页又一页，直到最后一页。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a heavy door that must be pushed open again at every stage.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一扇沉重的门，每到一个阶段都得再推一次。

abstract.en: Picture a person who keeps pursuing a goal after everyone else has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都停下之后，仍有一个人在追求那个目标。

examples.en: The state may prosecute only if the evidence meets a fixed standard.
examples.cn: 只有证据达到固定标准，州一方才可以起诉。

examples.en: They prosecuted him for fraud and lost the first hearing.
examples.cn: 他们以欺诈罪起诉他，却输掉了第一次庭审。

examples.en: The council prosecuted the inquiry for three years.
examples.cn: 委员会把这项调查进行了三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究」——把诉状剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的过去分词 prosecutus 的词干 prosecut-；由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from bringing a criminal charge, through conducting the case, pursuing a civil claim, carrying on an inquiry, pressing a war, executing a plan, following up an appeal, and pursuing a goal in literary style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从提起刑事指控开始，经推进案件、追究民事请求、进行调查、推进战争、执行计划、追究上诉，最后到文学文体中的执着追求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger walking down a numbered page to the last line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着编号的页面走到最后一行。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: the act starts a criminal case and then keeps it moving.
branches.cn: 指控：这个动作启动刑事案件，然后又不断把它往前推。

branches.en: THE CIVIL CLAIM: the same verb reaches claims that are not criminal at all.
branches.cn: 民事请求：同一个动词也覆盖完全不属于刑事的请求。

branches.en: THE FORMAL EFFORT: any inquiry, duty or plan can be carried forward.
branches.cn: 正式的努力：任何调查、职责或计划都可以被推行。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: wars and appeals are both pressed on to their next stage.
branches.cn: 推进：战争与上诉都被压向下一阶段。

branches.en: THE LITERARY EDGE: the same following motion becomes a picture of relentless ambition.
branches.cn: 文学边缘：同一个「追随」动作成了不知停歇的抱负图景。

intro.en: Prosecute is a verb built on a Latin participle stem, and its endings are what turn that stem into an English action word.
intro.cn: prosecute 是建立在拉丁分词词干上的动词，词尾把那个词干变成英语的动作词。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth', sequi 'follow' and the participle stem prosecut- are the pieces; English added the verb ending -e to make prosecute.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是 pro-「向前」、sequi「跟随」与分词词干 prosecut-；英语加上动词词尾 -e 构成 prosecute。

core_image: 一个人站在高处向前看，视线越过地平线，既看见眼前的景，也看见将要发生的事
scene: 年轻工程师站在黎明的山脊上，望着可能蕴藏矿藏的谷地。The prospect of finding copper in this valley is good.

senses.title: The future in view: what lies ahead
senses.titleCN: 前景：前方等待的那幅图景
senses.definition: the possibility or expectation of something happening in the future, especially something good
senses.definitionCN: 对未来某事的可能性或预期，尤指好事
senses.example: The prospect of a long winter worried the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长冬季的前景让农民们忧心。
senses.why: The noun appears in the 1660s as 'expectation, ground of expectation', from the habit of looking forward. What the eye does in space, the mind does in time: it scans the horizon of coming events.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 60 年代出现，义为“预期、期待的依据”，来自“向前看”的动作。眼睛在空间里做的事，心智在时间里也做：它扫视将要发生之事的地平线。

senses.title: A chance that may come true
senses.titleCN: 可能性、机会：尚未兑现的那份可能
senses.definition: a chance or possibility that something will happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或成功的可能性
senses.example: There is little prospect of finding survivors after so long.
senses.exampleCN: 过了这么久，找到幸存者的可能性很小。
senses.why: The 1620s sense 'mental view or survey' let people speak of viewing a future outcome. Once an outcome is 'in view', it is a chance on the horizon rather than a certainty in hand.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代“心中的审视”这一义项，让人可以“看见”未来的结果。一个结果一旦“在视野里”，它就是地平线上的机会，而不是握在手里的确定。

senses.title: The sweep of the eye: a wide view
senses.titleCN: 景象、视野：眼睛扫过的那一大片
senses.definition: a view or scene, especially a wide one seen from a high place
senses.definitionCN: 景色、景象，尤指从高处看到的广阔视野
senses.example: From the hilltop we had a fine prospect of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 从山顶上，我们看到了山谷的美丽景色。
senses.why: From 1530s English, prospect meant 'extensive view of the landscape', straight from Latin prospectus 'distant view'. The word still carries the physical sweep of the eye before it carries hope.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 30 年代起，prospect 指“广阔的风景视野”，直接来自拉丁语 prospectus“远处的景色”。这个词先有眼睛的物理扫视，后才有希望之义。

senses.title: Someone worth watching: the promising person
senses.titleCN: 潜在客户、有前途的人选：值得盯住的那个人
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as likely to succeed, or a possible customer or candidate
senses.definitionCN: 被认为可能成功的人或事物；潜在客户或候选人
senses.example: The agent spends her mornings calling new prospects.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经纪人每天上午给新潜在客户打电话。
senses.why: From 1922, prospect named 'a person or thing considered promising', out of the 1660s sense of expectation of advantage. A good customer is someone in whom the seller sees a future.
senses.whyCN: 从 1922 年起，prospect 指“被认为有前途的人或事物”，源自 17 世纪 60 年代“预期好处”的义项。好客户，就是卖方在其身上看得见未来的人。

senses.title: Grounds for hoping
senses.titleCN: 预期的依据：凭什么盼着
senses.definition: grounds for expecting something; a reasonable basis for anticipation
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的预期依据；合理的盼望理由
senses.example: The deal offers no prospect of profit this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易今年没有获利的指望。
senses.why: The 1660s sense was not the hope itself but its ground: 'expectation, ground of expectation'. The landscape metaphor persists — a prospect is what the situation lets you see coming.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 60 年代的义项不是希望本身，而是希望的依据：“预期、期待的依据”。风景的隐喻仍在：prospect 就是局势允许你看见的、即将到来的东西。

senses.title: Looking for ore: to prospect the ground
senses.definition: to search an area for gold, oil, or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区寻找黄金、石油或其他矿藏
senses.example: They prospected the valley for copper throughout the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在那个山谷里勘探铜矿。
senses.why: The verb dates from 1841, from a specialized 1832 noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore'. The miner literally looks out over the land to see what it promises.
senses.whyCN: 动词始于 1841 年，来自 1832 年的名词专义“有矿苗的地方”。矿工字面上就是在土地上四处张望，看它许诺了什么。

senses.title: Surveying the site before building
senses.titleCN: 勘察、探测：动工之前先看一遍
senses.definition: to examine land or a site, especially to judge its potential or value
senses.definitionCN: 勘查土地或场地，尤指评估其潜力或价值
senses.example: Engineers prospected the site before the dam was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝获批之前，工程师们勘察了坝址。
senses.why: English had an older verb prospect 'look forth, look out over' (1550s) from Latin prospectare, a frequentative of prospicere. The mining sense revived that old surveying gesture.
senses.whyCN: 英语早有动词 prospect“向外看、俯瞰”（16 世纪 50 年代），来自拉丁语 prospectare，是 prospicere 的反复体。采矿义让这个古老的勘看动作重新流行。

senses.title: A mental survey: the wide view of a subject
senses.titleCN: 宏观审视：把一门学问摊开来看
senses.definition: a broad mental view or survey of a subject, situation, or period
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题、局势或时期的宏观心理审视
senses.example: The book gives a broad prospect of a century of science.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对百年科学史作了宏观的审视。
senses.why: The transferred sense 'mental view or survey' is recorded from the 1620s. The eye's sweep over a valley becomes the mind's sweep over a field of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: “心中的视野/审视”这一转移义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代。眼睛扫过山谷的动作，变成了心智扫过一片知识领域。

senses.title: The long straight avenue
senses.titleCN: 大街、大道：一眼望不到头的那条路
senses.definition: a wide, straight street or avenue, especially in a Russian city
senses.definitionCN: 宽阔笔直的大街或大道，尤指俄罗斯城市中的
senses.example: Nevsky Prospect runs straight through the heart of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 涅瓦大街笔直地穿过城市中心。
senses.why: In 1866 English borrowed Russian prospekt 'avenue', which itself came from Latin prospectus. A grand avenue is a street designed to give the eye a long, uninterrupted prospect.
senses.whyCN: 1866 年英语借入俄语 prospekt“大街”，而俄语这个词又来自拉丁语 prospectus。宏伟的大道，就是一条为了让视线获得漫长而不中断的前景而设计的街。

intro.en: Prospect is one of the spec- words: all of them are about looking. Latin prospicere 'look forward' gives the noun prospectus 'a distant view', and English extends the same word from landscape to expectation, to customers, and finally to mining.
intro.cn: prospect 是 spec- 词族的一员：它们都与“看”有关。拉丁语 prospicere“向前看”给出名词 prospectus“远处的景色”，英语再把同一个词从风景扩展到预期、客户，最后扩展到采矿。

items.en: Prospicere meant 'to look out on, look forward', built from pro 'forward' plus specere 'to look at'. Specere goes back to PIE *spek- 'to observe', a reconstruction with no written record, so that deepest layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prospicere 意为“眺望、向前看”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成。specere 可追溯到印欧语 *spek-“观察”，但这是没有书面记录的重构，因此最深层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Prospectus, the past-participle stem used as a noun, meant 'distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight'. It named both the thing seen and the power of seeing it.
items.cn: prospectus 由过去分词词干用作名词，意为“远处的景色、眺望；视觉、视力”。它既指被看见之物，也指看见的能力。

items.en: The noun enters English as 'the act of looking into the distance; the condition of facing something or a certain direction'. The looking is still literal.
items.cn: 名词进入英语时意为“向远处看的动作；朝向某物或某个方向的状态”。这里的“看”仍是字面义。

items.en: The meaning widens to 'an extensive view of the landscape' (1530s), then to 'mental view or survey' (1620s), then to 'that which is presented to the eye, a scene' (1630s).
items.cn: 词义先扩展为“广阔的风景视野”（16 世纪 30 年代），再扩展为“心中的审视”（17 世纪 20 年代），又扩展为“呈现于眼前之物、景象”（17 世纪 30 年代）。

items.en: 'Expectation, ground of expectation, especially of advantage' appears in the 1660s on the notion of looking forward. From it come 'person or thing considered promising' (1922) and the plural prospects, 'things looked forward to'.
items.cn: “预期、期待的依据，尤指好处”于 17 世纪 60 年代出现，基于“向前看”的意象。由此派生出“被认为有前途的人或事物”（1922）以及复数 prospects“所期待之事”。

items.en: Mining uses a specialized noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore' (1832), and the verb 'explore for gold or minerals' follows in 1841, from prospect (n.).
items.cn: 采矿业先有名词专义“有矿苗的地点”（1832），动词“勘探黄金或矿物”于 1841 年随后出现，来自名词 prospect。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- look or the -spect shape; the meaning group shares the idea of a future chance, but not its spelling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec-“看”或 -spect 的外形；近义组共享“未来的机会”这一概念，但拼写不同。

entries.definition: a printed plan describing a school, company, or proposed enterprise. It is prospect plus the Latin noun ending -us.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍学校、公司或拟办事业的印刷章程。它就是 prospect 加上拉丁名词词尾 -us。

entries.definition: to look back at someone with esteem. It uses the same specere 'look' but with re- 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；回头看某人并怀有敬意。它用同一个 specere“看”，但前缀是 re-“向后”。

entries.definition: a person who watches an event. The root is pure 'look', with no pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 观众；旁观者。词根是纯粹的“看”，没有 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: a way of seeing things from a particular point. It looks through a situation rather than forward.
entries.definitionCN: 视角；透视法。它是透过一个情境去看，而不是向前看。

entries.definition: the likely future of a situation. It is the closest everyday synonym of prospect in the sense of expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 前景；展望。在“预期”这一义项上，它是最接近 prospect 的日常同义词。

entries.definition: the chance that something will happen. It measures probability, while prospect often adds hope or dread.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；或然性。它衡量概率，而 prospect 常带有希望或忧虑的色彩。

entries.definition: a long, wide view, especially between rows of trees. It matches the landscape sense of prospect.
entries.definitionCN: 远景；狭长的视野，尤指树列之间的。它对应 prospect 的风景义。

entries.definition: the act of expecting something and preparing for it. It names the mental act that prospect describes as a view.
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待。它命名的是 prospect 以“视野”来描绘的那种心理活动。

entries.definition: something that may exist or happen. It is neutral, where prospect usually implies evaluation.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；可能之事。它是中性的，而 prospect 通常含有评价意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin specere 'to look', the spec- family, and the mining and customer senses that grew from the same gaze.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 specere“看”、spec- 词族，以及从同一道目光里长出的采矿义和客户义。

normal.en: prospect = pro- 'forward' + spect 'look': to look forward is to see a prospect.
normal.cn: prospect = pro-“向前”+ spect“看”：向前看，看见的就是前景。

normal.en: The spec- family is all eyes: spectator, inspect, respect, perspective, circumspect.
normal.cn: spec- 词族全是眼睛：spectator、inspect、respect、perspective、circumspect。

normal.en: A prospectus is the same word in a brochure: a school lets you look ahead at what it offers.
normal.cn: prospectus 就是同一个词做成的小册子：学校让你提前看见它能提供什么。

normal.en: A prospector looks over the ground exactly as you look over the future.
normal.cn: prospector（勘探者）打量土地的样子，正像你打量未来。

normal.en: Job prospects are literally 'things looked forward to' in the plural.
normal.cn: job prospects 字面上就是复数形式的“被向前看的事情”。

abstract.en: Future is treated as a landscape: you stand here and scan what is coming.
abstract.cn: 未来被当作一片风景：你站在此处，扫视将要到来的一切。

abstract.en: Looking and hoping are one gesture in this word; the eye and the mind share a horizon.
abstract.cn: 在这个词里，看与盼是同一个动作；眼睛和心智共享一条地平线。

abstract.en: The word travels from landscape to time to market: a view, a chance, a customer.
abstract.cn: 这个词从风景走到时间，再走到市场：一片景、一个机会、一位客户。

examples.en: The prospect of moving abroad excited her more than it frightened her.
examples.cn: 移居国外的前景让她兴奋多过害怕。

examples.en: Geologists spent three years prospecting for oil in the desert.
examples.cn: 地质学家在沙漠里花了三年勘探石油。

examples.en: The sales team treats every inquiry as a potential prospect.
examples.cn: 销售团队把每一次询价都当作潜在客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ spect（看）——向前看，前景就在眼前；谐音“普罗斯佩克特”：普查（pro）一遍，向前看矿藏 → prospect 前景；勘探

root: 源自拉丁语 prospicere“向前看、眺望”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成，名词 prospectus 意为“远处的景色”；核心是“向前看所得到的那片景”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one gaze. The eye first sweeps a landscape, then the mind sweeps the future; what is seen becomes a chance, a customer, a subject surveyed, a street, and finally ground to be searched for ore.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一道目光。眼睛先扫过风景，心智再扫过未来；被看见的东西依次变成机会、客户、被审视的学科、一条大街，最后成为要去地下搜寻矿藏的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing high and looking forward — the view ahead, in space or in time.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处向前看——空间或时间中前方的那片景。

chain: SEE A CHANCE IN A PERSON

branches.en: THE EXPECTED FUTURE: prospect as what is anticipated, and the grounds for that anticipation.
branches.cn: 被期待的未来：作为预期内容的前景，以及支撑这份预期的依据。

branches.en: THE CHANCE AND THE PERSON: a possibility on the horizon, and someone in whom a future is seen.
branches.cn: 机会与人：地平线上的可能性，以及被人看见未来的人。

branches.en: THE WIDE VIEW: the landscape before the eyes, and the broad survey before the mind.
branches.cn: 广阔视野：眼前的风景，以及心智对学科的宏观审视。

branches.en: LOOKING INTO THE EARTH: mining for ore, and surveying a site for what it may yield.
branches.cn: 向地下看：探矿，以及为评估潜力而勘察场地。

branches.en: THE LONG AVENUE: a street built to give the eye an unbroken prospect.
branches.cn: 长长的大道：一条为了让视线获得不中断前景而建的街。

intro.en: Prospect is pro- plus spec- plus -t. Its family shows the prefix pro-, re-, per-, circum- and in-, the root spec- 'look', and the noun and agent endings -tus, -tor, -ive and -ion.
intro.cn: prospect 是 pro- 加 spec- 再加 -t。它的词族展示前缀 pro-、re-、per-、circum-、in-，词根 spec-“看”，以及名词与施事后缀 -tus、-tor、-ive、-ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look at' is the base of spectator, inspect and respect; with prefixes it yields prospicere, respicere, perspicere and circumspicere, and the noun prospectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere“看”是 spectator、inspect、respect 的基础；加前缀又给出 prospicere、respicere、perspicere、circumspicere，以及名词 prospectus。

items.meaning: a view ahead; expectation; to search the ground
items.example: The prospect of promotion kept her working late.
items.exampleCN: 升职的前景让她一直工作到很晚。

items.example: Officials came to inspect the factory.
items.exampleCN: 官员们来检查这家工厂。

items.meaning: to look back at with esteem
items.example: Students respect a teacher who listens.
items.exampleCN: 学生尊敬愿意倾听的老师。

items.example: The stadium held fifty thousand spectators.
items.exampleCN: 体育场容纳了五万名观众。

items.meaning: a way of seeing through a scene
items.example: Travel gives you a new perspective on home.
items.exampleCN: 旅行让你对家乡有了新的视角。

items.meaning: to look out mentally; to guess or invest
items.example: Reporters speculated about the reason for her resignation.
items.exampleCN: 记者们推测她辞职的原因。

items.meaning: the side something presents to the eye
items.meaningCN: 方面；外观（看过去的那一面）
items.example: We discussed every aspect of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 我们讨论了计划的每个方面。

items.meaningCN: 谨慎的（四周看遍再行动）
items.example: She was circumspect in accepting the offer.
items.exampleCN: 她在接受这个提议时很谨慎。

items.meaning: looking inward at one's own mind
items.example: His diary is a record of quiet introspection.
items.exampleCN: 他的日记是一份安静内省的记录。

items.meaning: a printed plan that lets you look ahead
items.meaningCN: 章程；招股书（让人预先看清全貌）
items.example: The university's prospectus lists every course.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学的章程列出了每一门课程。

latinEntries.meaning: to look forward, look out on

definition_zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；富足；顺境
definition_en: the condition of being successful and growing, especially when a country, region or business has rising income, trade and well-being
core_image: 粮仓一格格装满，账本上的数字连年往上走
scene: 港口重新修好的那几年，小城的码头上又挤满了货船，店铺一家接一家开张。In the years after the harbour was rebuilt, prosperity returned to the little town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperity 表示「经济繁荣、兴旺」（第 1 个义项：地区经济向上走）；句意为港口重建后的几年里，繁荣又回到了这座小城。

pos.zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；顺境

derivatives.zh: prosper 加 -ous 构成形容词，把「兴旺」写成一种性质
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 再加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economic success and growth
senses.definition: the condition in which a country or region grows richer, with rising trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 国家或地区越来越富裕，贸易、收入与就业都在上升的状态
senses.example: The port brought prosperity to the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口给整个地区带来了繁荣。
senses.why: Prosperity first names the visible sign of a hope that came true: warehouses full, ships coming in, wages paid. Because the Latin stem joins a forward direction to hope, the word naturally settles on growth you can see in a harbour or a market.
senses.whyCN: prosperity 最初指的是希望兑现之后看得见的迹象：仓库堆满、船只进港、工钱按时发放。它的拉丁词干把「朝前」和「希望」绑在一起，所以这个词自然落在港口与市场上看得见的增长。

senses.title: Personal success and good fortune
senses.definition: the state of doing well in one's life or career, with things going favourably
senses.definitionCN: 在人生或事业上走得顺，事情朝着有利方向发展的状态
senses.example: He attributed his prosperity to patience and a little luck.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的成功归功于耐心和一点运气。
senses.why: A hope placed in front of a country can also be placed in front of one person: when plans keep working out, the same word names a private run of good years rather than a national boom.
senses.whyCN: 放在一个国家前面的希望，也能放在一个人前面：当计划一件件走通，同一个词就从国家层面的景气转到私人生活里的一段好年景。

senses.title: A period of thriving
senses.definition: a stretch of years in which business and living standards are strong, seen as a period one can date
senses.definitionCN: 生意与生活水平都很强劲的一段年头，可以被标出起止时间
senses.example: The decades of prosperity ended abruptly with the war.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的繁荣随着战争戛然而止。
senses.why: A boom has a beginning and an end, so the word can be counted and dated; it then names the years themselves, not a permanent condition.
senses.whyCN: 景气有开头也有结尾，所以这个词可以被计数、被标出年份；这时它指的是那几年本身，而不是一种永久状态。

senses.title: Material wealth; affluence
senses.definition: great wealth, especially as shown in comfortable living conditions and possessions
senses.definitionCN: 大量财富，尤指体现在舒适生活条件与财物上的富足
senses.example: They lived in prosperity, but never talked about money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们日子过得很富足，却从不谈钱。
senses.why: Seen through a household rather than a nation, the same state turns into furniture, food and leisure, so the word comes to mean the wealth itself rather than the growth that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 若从一户人家而不是一个国家的角度去看，同一种状态就变成家具、饭菜与闲暇，于是这个词指的是财富本身，而不是产生财富的那段增长。

senses.title: Favourable conditions; good fortune
senses.definition: favourable circumstances or good luck, especially in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 有利的境况或好运气，多见于较早或文学性的用法
senses.example: He wished them health and prosperity in the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 他祝他们来年健康顺遂。
senses.why: Before economics took the word over, it covered any favourable turn of events; the old blessing formula keeps that wider sense alive in toasts and greetings.
senses.whyCN: 在经济学接管这个词之前，它泛指任何有利的转折；祝酒与贺词里那套古老的祝福语，把这层更宽的意味保留了下来。

intro.en: Prosperity comes from Latin prosperitas, a noun built on prosperus, which is usually analysed as pro- 'forward' plus spes 'hope'.
intro.cn: prosperity 来自拉丁语 prosperitas，其基础是 prosperus；一般认为它由 pro-「向前」加 spes「希望」构成。

items.en: Spes meant hope. The picture behind it is a hope set in front of a person, something to walk toward.
items.cn: spes 意为希望。它背后的画面是把希望摆在人的前面，让人朝它走去。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes gave prosperus, 'favourable, fortunate'. This is the usual analysis; the exact formation is still debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 得到 prosperus，意为「顺利的、吉利的」。这是通常的分析，但具体构词细节仍有讨论。

items.en: Prosperitas named favourable fortune and success, the abstract state behind the adjective.
items.cn: prosperitas 指顺遂的运气与成功，是把那个形容词变成抽象状态的名称。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prosperite, meaning success and well-being, and English took it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 prosperite，意为成功与安好，英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperity covers national economies, private wealth and any run of good years.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperity 覆盖国家经济、私人财富以及任何一段顺遂的年头。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family around spes; the near-meaning group collects words for wealth and growth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 spes 这一拉丁词族展开；近义组收表示财富与增长的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same stem, describing someone or something that is doing well.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词，形容人或事物兴旺、发达。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed or to do well, the base of both the noun and the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为兴旺、发达，是名词与形容词共同的词干。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a successful or wealthy way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为兴旺地、富足地。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the quality of being prosperous.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的名词，指兴旺、富足的性质。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 大量钱财与财物；财富。

entries.definition: A period when trade and business grow quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 商业迅速增长的时期；景气。

entries.definition: The state of having plenty of money and comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与舒适生活的状态；富足。

entries.definition: The achievement of a goal, or of fame and money.
entries.definitionCN: 达到目标，或获得名声与财富；成功。

normalIntro.en: Most of the word is carried by two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, and by the English suffixes that turn the verb prosper into a state.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词大半由两个拉丁成分撑起：pro- 与 spes，再加上把动词 prosper 变成状态名词的英语后缀。

normal.en: Pro- means forward and spes means hope, so prosperity is hope that has moved in front of you and come true.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，所以 prosperity 是「被放到你前面并且兑现了的希望」。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb underneath: a person prospers, and prosperity is the state that results.
normal.cn: 底下的动词是 prosper：人先兴旺起来，prosperity 是随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The suffix -ity turns an adjective into a state, the same way able becomes ability.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成状态，就像 able 变成 ability 一样。

normal.en: The Latin hope word spes also hides in desperate, where de- means without, so desperate is literally 'without hope'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的希望 spes 还藏在 desperate 里：de- 表示「没有」，desperate 字面就是「没有希望」。

normal.en: Learn it inside the phrase economic prosperity, because the word is used most often about countries and regions.
normal.cn: 把它放在 economic prosperity 这个词组里记，因为它最常用来谈国家与地区。

abstract.en: Picture storehouses that are a little fuller each year: prosperity is the direction of the line, not a single good harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一排粮仓，每年都比上一年满一点：繁荣是那条线的方向，而不是一次好收成。

abstract.en: A boom can end, so the word often takes a period word beside it, as in a decade of prosperity.
abstract.cn: 景气会结束，所以这个词旁边常带一个表示时间段的词，例如十年繁荣。

abstract.en: Shared prosperity asks whether the growth reaches ordinary tables, which is why the phrase carries moral weight.
abstract.cn: 共享繁荣问的是增长有没有落到普通人的餐桌上，这也是这个说法带有道德分量的原因。

examples.en: The new railway brought prosperity to villages that had been cut off for centuries.
examples.cn: 新铁路给那些与外界隔绝了几个世纪的村庄带来了繁荣。

examples.en: Economists still argue about how long the present prosperity can last.
examples.cn: 经济学家仍在争论当前的繁荣能持续多久。

examples.en: His prosperity began with a small workshop behind the family house.
examples.cn: 他的兴旺始于自家屋后的一间小作坊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「铺路拾贝提」：先把路铺好，再拾到贝壳，最后提到货，一路忙下来，家业就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其名词 prosperitas 经古法语 prosperite 进入英语。一般认为这一词源分析成立，但 prosperus 的具体构词仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hoped-for turn that really goes well; from that one idea grow economic boom, personal success, a dated period of good years, material comfort and the older sense of good fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「盼来的转机真的变好」；由这一个念头长出经济繁荣、个人成功、可数的一段好年景、物质富足，以及较早的「好运、顺境」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: granaries filling up year after year while the ledger totals climb.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓一年比一年满，账本上的总数不断往上走。

branches.en: a harbour where loaded ships keep arriving and wages are paid on time
branches.cn: 货船不断进港、工钱按时发放的港口

branches.en: a man reading a good annual report at his desk
branches.cn: 一个人坐在桌前读一份漂亮的年报

branches.en: a stretch of good years marked on a timeline
branches.cn: 时间轴上被标出的一段好年头

branches.en: a warm house with a full table
branches.cn: 桌上摆满饭菜的暖屋子

branches.en: a New Year toast raised in a hall
branches.cn: 大厅里举起的祝酒

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, plus a noun suffix explain how a hope becomes a verb, a state and a description.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分 pro- 与 spes，加上名词后缀，解释了「希望」如何变成动词、状态名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around spes is well recorded: a noun for hope, a verb for hoping, and the prosperus words for good fortune.
latinIntro.cn: spes 周围的拉丁词族有清楚记录：表示希望的名词、表示期盼的动词，以及表示好运的 prosperus 一族。

items.example: The small firm began to prosper.
items.exampleCN: 这家小公司开始兴旺起来。

definition_zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的
definition_en: doing well and growing strong, especially in economic terms; wealthy and successful
core_image: 码头上吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯一直亮到深夜
scene: 铁路修通以后，原本安静的村子盖起了砖房，集市从清晨一直热闹到天黑。Within a decade the quiet village had become a prosperous trading town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperous 是「繁荣的、兴旺的」（第 1 个义项：经济上有活力）；句意为十年之内，那个安静的村子变成了繁荣的贸易城镇。

pos.zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的

derivatives.zh: prosperous 把 -ous 换成 -ity，得到「繁荣」这一状态名词
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economically strong and growing
senses.definition: having a strong economy, with growing trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 经济强劲、贸易、收入与就业都在增长的
senses.example: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the noun's outward signs but attaches them to a place: a town is prosperous when its cranes, ships and wages all point the same way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了名词那套看得见的迹象，只是把它们贴到一个地方身上：吊塔、船只与工资都朝同一个方向走，这座城就是繁荣的。

senses.title: Making money; financially successful
senses.definition: doing well in business and earning a good income
senses.definitionCN: 生意做得顺、收入可观的
senses.example: She runs a prosperous little bakery near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近经营一家生意兴隆的小面包店。
senses.why: The suffix -ous turns the state into a quality, so the word can sit straight on a shop or a firm that keeps earning; growth is now read in takings rather than in the size of a region.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 把状态变成一种性质，于是这个词可以直接贴到一家持续赚钱的店铺或公司上；这时增长是从营业额里读出来的，而不是从地区规模里读出来的。

senses.title: Wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: rich enough to live comfortably, especially of a person or a family
senses.definitionCN: 钱财足以过得舒适，尤指人或家庭
senses.example: Their prosperous neighbours lent them the money for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们富裕的邻居借钱给他们修屋顶。
senses.why: Applied to people, the same quality shifts from output to comfort: what shows is not trade figures but a full table, warm rooms and the spare money that can be lent to a neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 用到人身上，同一种性质就从产出转向舒适：显出来的不是贸易数字，而是一桌饭菜、暖和的房间，以及能借给邻居的余钱。

senses.title: Successful and favourable; thriving
senses.definition: doing well or likely to do well; favourable, especially of a period or an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 走得顺或可望走顺的；有利的，尤指一段时间或一项事业
senses.example: The firm entered a prosperous season after the treaty was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订之后，这家公司进入了一段顺遂的时期。
senses.why: The oldest Latin layer meant favourable or lucky, and that colour returns when the word describes a period or a plan rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的拉丁义层是「顺遂的、吉利的」，当这个词形容一段时间或一个计划而不是一个地方时，那层意味就回来了。

intro.en: Prosperous is the Latin adjective prosperus, built on pro- 'forward' and spes 'hope', and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: prosperous 就是拉丁形容词 prosperus，由 pro-「向前」与 spes「希望」构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Spes was the noun for hope, and the image behind it is a hope set in front of the eyes.
items.cn: spes 是表示希望的名词，背后的画面是把希望摆在眼前。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes formed prosperus, meaning favourable or fortunate; this is the usual analysis, though the details are debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 构成 prosperus，意为顺遂的、吉利的；这是通常的分析，细节仍有争议。

items.en: The verb prosperare meant to thrive or to make something thrive, and it fed both the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 动词 prosperare 意为兴旺、使兴旺，同时供养了形容词与名词。

items.en: Old French used prospere for fortunate and successful, and Middle English borrowed it in that shape.
items.cn: 古法语用 prospere 表示顺遂、成功，中古英语以这个形态借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperous describes economies, businesses, families and favourable periods, keeping the -ous adjective beside the -ity noun.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperous 可形容经济、企业、家庭与顺遂的时期，并让 -ous 结尾的形容词与 -ity 结尾的名词并排存在。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spes family and one near-spelling; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for wealth and healthy growth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spes 词族，并收一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示富裕与健康增长的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of doing well, formed with -ity where the adjective has -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，形容词用 -ous 结尾，名词用 -ity 结尾。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed and grow strong.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为兴旺、发达。

entries.definition: The adverb formed by adding -ly to this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -ly 构成的副词，意为兴旺地。

entries.definition: Only the spelling is close; this word means false and comes from Latin spurius, so the two are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，这个词意为虚假的，来自拉丁语 spurius，两者并无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: Growing strongly and doing well.
entries.definitionCN: 茁壮成长、势头很好的。

entries.definition: Having a lot of money and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与财物的。

entries.definition: Developing well and spreading strongly, often of plants, arts or business.
entries.definitionCN: 发展得好、势头旺盛的，常用于植物、艺术或生意。

entries.definition: Growing very fast, especially of trade or prices.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速增长的，尤指贸易或价格。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin adjective prosperus in English dress: pro- 'forward', spes 'hope', and the suffix -ous that makes a quality out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是换上英语外衣的拉丁形容词 prosperus：pro-「向前」、spes「希望」，以及把二者变成性质的 -ous。

normal.en: Pro- is forward, spes is hope, and -ous turns the pair into a quality, so prosperous describes something that hope has favoured.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，-ous 把这一对变成性质，所以 prosperous 形容被希望照顾到的事物。

normal.en: The noun twin is prosperity: -ous marks the adjective, -ity marks the noun, and the stem never changes.
normal.cn: 名词搭档是 prosperity：-ous 标记形容词，-ity 标记名词，词干始终不变。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb in the middle: prosperity and prosperous are both built on it, one as a state and one as a quality.
normal.cn: 中间的动词是 prosper：prosperity 与 prosperous 都建在它上面，一个表状态，一个表性质。

normal.en: Desperate shares the Latin hope word spes but adds de- 'without', so the two words pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: desperate 共享拉丁语的希望 spes，但加上 de-「没有」，所以这两个词的方向正好相反。

normal.en: Note the spelling: the ending is -ous, not -ious, so there is no extra i before the u.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：结尾是 -ous 而不是 -ious，u 前面并没有多余的 i。

abstract.en: Think of a street where every second shutter is open and the lamps stay on late: that is prosperity seen as a quality.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，隔一家店就开着门，灯亮到很晚：这就是被看成一种性质的繁荣。

abstract.en: Add -ous and the word points at a thing; add -ity and it points at a condition. The suffix decides the grammar, not the meaning.
abstract.cn: 加 -ous，词就指向事物；加 -ity，词就指向状态。后缀决定语法角色，不决定意思。

abstract.en: A prosperous year and a year of prosperity say the same thing, one as a label and one as a period you can count.
abstract.cn: 「繁荣的一年」与「一段繁荣」说的是同一件事，一个像标签，一个像可以数出来的时间段。

examples.en: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。

examples.en: A prosperous town needs more than one good year.
examples.cn: 一座繁荣的城镇需要的远不止一个丰收年。

examples.en: They moved to a prosperous suburb with better schools.
examples.cn: 他们搬到了一个学校更好的富裕郊区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普罗斯珀勒斯」：先铺路，再拾珀，最后把家业勒紧攒起来，日子就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其动词 prosperare 意为兴旺；形容词经古法语 prospere 进入英语。一般认为词源分析成立，构词细节仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses keep the same picture of things going well; they differ only in where the success is read: a place, a business, a household, or a stretch of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项保留同一幅「事情顺利」的画面，区别只在于从哪里读出成功：一个地方、一门生意、一户人家，或一段时间。

core.cn: 核心意象：繁忙码头上的吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯亮到深夜。

branches.en: a skyline of cranes above a working port
branches.cn: 工作港口上空的吊塔群

branches.en: a shop with a queue at the counter
branches.cn: 柜台前排着队的店铺

branches.en: a family eating in a warm dining room
branches.cn: 一家人在暖和的餐厅里吃饭

branches.en: a plan that keeps working out
branches.cn: 一步步走通的计划

branches.en: a town that stays lucky for years
branches.cn: 连续多年走运的城镇

intro.en: The stem is Latin; the two endings -ous and -ity do the English work of splitting quality from state.
intro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语；-ous 与 -ity 这两个结尾在英语里分工，一个表性质，一个表状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin recorded spes for hope, prosperus for fortunate, and prosperare for making something thrive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语留下了 spes（希望）、prosperus（顺遂的）与 prosperare（使兴旺）这几个形式。

items.exampleCN: 这门生意开始兴旺起来。

definition_zh: 抗议；抗议活动；反对；申辩；坚称
definition_en: a public statement or action showing strong disagreement, the act of objecting in public, or a firm declaration that something is true
core_image: 一群人举着写满字的纸牌站在门前，谁都不肯散去
scene: 新规定贴出来的第二天清晨，居民们举着纸牌站到办公楼前，没有人愿意走开。Hundreds of residents gathered outside the office to protest against the new rule.
sceneCN: 这里表示「抗议、反对」（第 2 个义项：公开表达强烈反对）；句意为数百名居民聚在办公楼外，抗议这条新规定。

pos.zh: 抗议；抗议活动；异议
抗议；反对；申辩；坚称

derivatives.zh: 由 protest 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，义为「抗议者」
由拉丁词干 protestat- 加 -ion 构成，义为「声明；抗议」，语气正式
由 protesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着抗议地；不服地」

senses.title: A public expression of strong disagreement
senses.definition: a statement, gathering or march by which people show in public that they refuse to accept a decision or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 人们用声明、集会或游行的方式，公开表示不接受某项决定或某种状况
senses.example: The sit-in was a quiet protest against the closure of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 那次静坐是对关闭图书馆的一场无声抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to declare something publicly and call others to witness it; when the declaration is a refusal, the noun becomes the event in the street.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为公开声明并请人作证；当声明的内容是「不接受」时，名词就成了街头上的那场活动。

senses.title: To state in public that one objects
senses.definition: to say openly, often together with others, that something is wrong and ought to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出自己认为某事不对、应当改变，常与众人一起
senses.example: Villagers protested against the plan to dam the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民抗议在河上筑坝的计划。
senses.why: The same public declaration is now seen as an action rather than an event, so the verb keeps the crowd and the refusal but adds the doing.
senses.whyCN: 同一场公开声明被看成动作而不是事件，于是动词保留了人群与拒绝，只是多了一层「正在做」。

senses.title: To insist firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to say firmly that something is the case, especially when denying a charge or correcting what others believe
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地说某事就是这样，尤用于否认指控或纠正别人的看法
senses.example: He protested that he had never signed the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称自己从未签过那份文件。
senses.why: Before it meant to object, the Latin verb simply meant to bear witness; that older layer survives whenever a person protests innocence rather than protesting a policy.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「反对」之前，这个拉丁动词只表示「作证」；一个人申辩自己无罪而不是抗议某项政策时，留下的正是那更早的一层。

intro.en: Protest goes back to a Latin verb for bearing witness in public; English first used it for a solemn declaration and only later for a refusal.
intro.cn: protest 可追到拉丁语中「公开作证」的动词；英语最初用它指郑重的声明，后来才用来指拒绝接受。

items.en: Testis meant a witness, the person who can stand up and say what happened.
items.cn: testis 意为证人，即那个能站出来说出发生了什么的人。

items.en: Testari meant to bear witness or to call someone as a witness, and it grew out of testis.
items.cn: testari 意为作证或请人作证，由 testis 派生而来。

items.en: With pro-, the witnessing moved into the open, so protestari meant to declare something publicly and solemnly.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，作证被推到公开场合，于是 protestari 意为公开而郑重地声明。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as protest, a solemn declaration, and passed it into English around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语借入后写作 protest，意为郑重声明，约在十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: English kept the old sense of declaring, then added the modern one of objecting in public, and finally the quieter sense of insisting that one is right.
items.cn: 英语保留了「声明」的旧义，又添上「公开反对」的新义，最后还有「坚称自己没错」这层更安静的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin witness and the declaration built on it; the second group gathers words for objecting and for stating a grievance.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁语的「证人」及由此构成的「声明」；第二组收表示反对与诉说不满的词。

entries.definition: A formal declaration, especially one that objects to something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的声明，尤指表示反对的声明。

entries.definition: To give evidence as a witness, from the same Latin word for witness.
entries.definitionCN: 作为证人提供证词，出自同一个表示「证人」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A formal statement given by a witness in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证人在法庭上作出的正式陈述。

entries.definition: To keep someone safe; the prefix pro- is shared, but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某人；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To say that you disagree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意某事。

entries.definition: To gather in public in order to show opposition or support.
entries.definitionCN: 公开聚集以表示反对或支持。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong, often made to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指出某事有问题的说法，常向当局提出。

entries.definition: A loud public expression of anger or disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 公众大声表达的愤怒或不满。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the Latin witness: someone stands up in the open and says what he or she will not accept or will not admit.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都留着那个拉丁语的「证人」：有人站到明处，说出自己不接受或不承认的事。

normal.en: Pro- means forth and testis means witness, so protest is to bring a witness's statement out into public.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前、公开，testis 意为证人，所以 protest 就是把证人的话拿到公开场合说出来。

normal.en: Testify, testimony and protest all keep that witness, which is why a courtroom and a street march can share one root.
normal.cn: testify、testimony 与 protest 都保留着这个「证人」，所以法庭与街头游行能共用一个词根。

normal.en: The noun names the event and the verb names the doing, yet both need other people to hear the refusal.
normal.cn: 名词指那场活动，动词指正在做的动作，但两者都需要别人听见这份拒绝。

normal.en: Protesting that you are innocent keeps the oldest sense, because there the word is still a declaration rather than a complaint.
normal.cn: 申辩自己无罪保留的是最古老的那层意思，因为那里它仍是声明，而不是抱怨。

normal.en: The stress moves with the part of speech in British English, and that shift alone tells a listener whether the word is the event or the act.
normal.cn: 英式英语里重音随词性移动，单是这一变化就能让听者知道这个词指事件还是动作。

abstract.en: A protest asks to be heard before it asks to be obeyed, which is why it lives in the open air.
abstract.cn: 抗议先求被听见，才求被采纳，所以它总发生在露天的场所。

abstract.en: The same word covers refusal and declaration because both are a person standing up and saying what is true for them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指拒绝与声明，因为两者都是同一个人站出来，说出对他而言为真的事。

abstract.en: When a protest is ignored it tends to grow louder, while a declaration that is believed goes quiet, and one word holds both ends.
abstract.cn: 抗议被忽视时往往更响，声明被相信时反而安静，同一个词却装着这两端。

examples.en: Thousands joined the protest outside the town hall.
examples.cn: 数千人参加了市政厅外的抗议。

examples.en: They protested against the rise in bus fares.
examples.cn: 他们抗议公交车票价上涨。

examples.en: She protested that she had never met him.
examples.cn: 她坚称自己从未见过他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若泰斯特」——声音先「普」地一下炸开，再「泰斯特」地念出不满；记住 protest 是抗议、反对。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ testis（证人）→ testari（作证）→ protestari（公开声明、郑重宣称）→ 古法语 protest，约十四世纪进入英语。最早指「郑重声明」，后来才指「公开反对」。注意 protest 与 protect 只共用前缀 pro-：protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），protest 的词根是 testis（证人）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; the senses divide into the event of objecting, the act of objecting, and the older sense of insisting on the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；义项由此分出作为事件的抗议、作为动作的反对，以及更古老的「坚称事实」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding signs in front of a door, saying aloud what they will not accept.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人举着纸牌站在门前，把不肯接受的事大声说出来。

branches.en: a row of signs lifted above a crowd
branches.cn: 人群上方举起的一排纸牌

branches.en: a chant rising outside a closed office
branches.cn: 紧闭的办公楼外响起整齐的喊声

branches.en: a man repeating that he never signed
branches.cn: 一个人反复说自己从未签过字

branches.en: one refusal spoken and acted at the same time
branches.cn: 同一份拒绝既被说出又被行动

branches.en: a word that objects and a word that swears
branches.cn: 一个既在反对又在申明的词

intro.en: A Latin noun for witness, a prefix that brings the statement into public, and the English endings that make the doer and the formal noun hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「证人」的拉丁名词、把声明带到公开场合的前缀，以及造出「人」与正式名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Testis, testari and protestari are the reliable Latin cognates; the same witness root also appears in testimony and testify.
latinIntro.cn: testis、testari 与 protestari 是可靠的同源词；同一个「证人」词根也出现在 testimony 与 testify 里。

definition_zh: 质子；原子核中带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子；氢原子核
definition_en: a stable particle found in every atomic nucleus, carrying one unit of positive electric charge
core_image: 一颗带正电的小球被一层中和的云裹着，云散开后它独自露出来，仍牢牢占着中心的位置
scene: 云室里，宇宙射线留下一条粗短的白色轨迹。A proton knocked loose by a cosmic ray left a thick track in the cloud chamber.
sceneCN: 这里 proton 指「原子核中带正电的粒子」（第 1 个义项：原子核内带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子）；句意：一个被宇宙射线撞出的质子在云室里留下一条粗而短的轨迹。图中可辨识物件：云室、铅板、白色轨迹、实验台。

pos.zh: 质子（可数）

derivatives.zh: 质子的；与质子有关的
使质子化；向分子加入质子
质子化过程
反质子

senses.title: The positive particle of the nucleus
senses.titleCN: 原子核中带正电的粒子
senses.definition: the stable particle that carries one unit of positive charge inside an atomic nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 原子核内部带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子
senses.example: Every nucleus except ordinary hydrogen holds at least one proton.
senses.exampleCN: 除普通氢以外，每一种原子核都至少含有一个质子。
senses.why: The Greek name means 'first', and the proton was the first nuclear particle to be identified, so it took that name.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本义为「第一」，而质子是最早被辨认出的核内粒子，因此得了这个名字。

senses.title: A hydrogen nucleus on its own
senses.definition: a hydrogen nucleus stripped of its electron, which is exactly one proton
senses.definitionCN: 失去电子后的氢原子核，也就是单独的一个质子
senses.example: Strip the electron from a hydrogen atom and only a proton remains.
senses.exampleCN: 把电子从氢原子上剥离，剩下的就只有质子。
senses.why: Hydrogen is the one element whose nucleus is a single proton, so the general name also names that simplest case.
senses.whyCN: 氢是唯一核内只有一个质子的元素，因此这个通名也直接指最简单的那个情形。

senses.title: The count that fixes an element
senses.titleCN: 决定元素身份的那个数量
senses.definition: the number of protons in a nucleus, which determines which chemical element it is
senses.definitionCN: 原子核中的质子数目，决定它属于哪种化学元素
senses.example: Add one proton and the element changes into the next one in the table.
senses.exampleCN: 增加一个质子，元素就变成周期表里的下一种。
senses.why: A chemical reaction may move electrons but never changes this count, so the count became the identity card of an element.
senses.whyCN: 化学反应可以搬动电子，却改不了这个数目，于是这个数目成了元素的身份证明。

senses.title: A hydrogen ion in acid chemistry
senses.titleCN: 酸化学里被交出的氢离子
senses.definition: a bare hydrogen ion that an acid gives away to another substance
senses.definitionCN: 酸交给另一种物质的裸氢离子
senses.example: In the modern definition, an acid is any substance that can give up a proton.
senses.exampleCN: 按现代定义，凡能交出一个质子的物质都是酸。
senses.why: A hydrogen ion without its electron is a proton, so chemistry borrowed the nuclear name for the thing an acid hands over.
senses.whyCN: 失去电子的氢离子就是一个质子，因此化学界借用了核物理的称呼，来指酸交出的那个东西。

senses.title: A beam aimed at a tumour
senses.titleCN: 用于治疗肿瘤的质子束
senses.definition: a stream of accelerated protons used as a medical tool that can be stopped at a chosen depth
senses.definitionCN: 把质子加速成束，作为能在选定深度停下的医疗工具
senses.example: The clinic chose proton treatment because the beam stops inside the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所选用质子治疗，因为粒子束会在肿瘤内部停下。
senses.why: Protons lose energy in a predictable way, so a beam can be aimed to spare the healthy tissue behind it.
senses.whyCN: 质子的能量损失有可预测的规律，因此束流可以被瞄准，从而避开其后方的健康组织。

senses.title: A fast visitor from space
senses.titleCN: 从太空高速到访的质子
senses.definition: a high-energy proton arriving from outer space as part of cosmic radiation
senses.definitionCN: 作为宇宙辐射的一部分，从外层空间高速抵达的高能质子
senses.example: A single cosmic proton can trigger a shower of secondary particles.
senses.exampleCN: 一个宇宙质子就能引发一连串次级粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are mostly protons, so astronomy uses the ordinary nuclear word for these travellers.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线主要由质子组成，天文学便用这个平常的核物理词来称呼这些远行者。

senses.title: The charged stream of the solar wind
senses.titleCN: 太阳风里的带电粒子流
senses.definition: one of the charged particles that the sun continuously sends out into space
senses.definitionCN: 太阳持续抛向太空的带电粒子之一
senses.example: The solar wind is a thin gas of protons and electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳风是质子与电子组成的稀薄气体。
senses.why: The solar wind is ionized hydrogen, so its positive half is simply protons.
senses.whyCN: 太阳风是电离的氢，其中带正电的那一半就是质子。

senses.title: The fuel of the proton chain in stars
senses.definition: a proton taking part in the fusion chain that powers stars like the sun
senses.definitionCN: 参与聚变链式反应、为太阳这类恒星供能的质子
senses.example: Four protons must combine before one helium nucleus appears in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 在太阳内部，要四个质子合起来才会出现一个氦核。
senses.why: The chain of reactions begins with protons, so the whole stellar process is named after them.
senses.whyCN: 这条反应链从质子开始，因此整个恒星过程以它命名。

intro.en: Proton is Greek, built from prōtos 'first' with the particle ending -on that physics later fixed in place. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语词，由「第一」加粒子命名惯用的词尾构成；年代均为约数。

items.en: Prōtos meant 'first, foremost', built on pro 'before, in front'. Its deeper origin is not reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前的」，由表示「在前」的成分构成。它更早的来源无法稳妥地重构。

items.en: The neuter form prōton meant 'the first thing'. Ancient writers used it for a first principle, long before physics existed.
items.cn: 中性形式 prōton 意为「第一者」。古代作者用它指第一原理，远在物理学出现之前。

items.en: When the lightest nucleus was identified around 1919 to 1920, the old word for a first thing was revived for it.
items.cn: 大约在 1919 至 1920 年间最轻的核被确认时，这个表示「第一者」的旧词被重新启用。

items.en: As the neutron was named by contrast, the positive partner kept the name proton, and the pair became the two nucleons.
items.cn: 中子作为对照被命名后，带正电的搭档保留质子之名，两者合称核子。

items.en: The first recorded uses for the modern particle sense are approximate; the word itself is ancient, the meaning is about a century old.
items.cn: 现代粒子义的最早书证年代为约数；词本身古老，而这一含义只有约一百年。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to proton but come from other roots; group two holds the particles it is measured against.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近却另有词源的词；第二组是常与它相比较的其他粒子。

entries.definition: From Greek phōs, phōtos 'light' plus the same particle ending: a quantum of light, with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「光」加同一个粒子结尾构成：光的一个量子，完全不带电荷。

entries.definition: Coined from Greek prōteios 'primary', which rests on the same prōtos 'first': a primary substance of living tissue, not a particle.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「首要的」造出，而这个词又出自同一个「第一」：指生命组织的首要成分，与粒子无关。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus agōnistēs 'competitor': the leading figure in a drama, from the same first-word root.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「竞争者」：戏剧中的首要人物，与质子的「第一」同源。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus typos 'impression': the first model of a thing, not a nuclear particle.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「印痕」：某物的首个模型，与核粒子无关。

entries.definition: The nucleon with almost the same mass and no electric charge; proton and neutron together make up nearly all nuclear mass.
entries.definitionCN: 质量几乎相同但不带电的核子；质子与中子共同构成几乎全部核质量。

entries.definition: The light negative particle that orbits the nucleus; its charge balances the proton's charge in a neutral atom.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕原子核运动的轻质负电粒子；在中性原子里，它的电荷与质子相抵。

entries.definition: The covering word for either kind of nuclear particle, so a proton is one sort of nucleon.
entries.definitionCN: 对两种核内粒子的统称，因此质子是核子的一种。

entries.definition: A whole atom or molecule that has gained or lost electrons; a lone proton is the smallest positive ion.
entries.definitionCN: 获得或失去电子的整个原子或分子；单独的质子是最小的正离子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek prōtos 'first' plus the particle ending -on: the first particle of the nucleus.
normal.cn: 希腊语「第一」加粒子结尾：核内第一个被认出的粒子。

normal.en: The proton sets the element's number, so its count is the identity of the atom.
normal.cn: 质子数决定元素，因此这个数目就是原子的身份。

normal.en: The family runs proton, protonic, protonate, protonation, antiproton.
normal.cn: 同族词包括质子、质子的、使质子化、质子化、反质子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: proton beam, proton therapy, proton donor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：质子束、质子治疗、质子供体。

normal.en: The same first-root appears in protein, protagonist and prototype, all from Greek prōtos.
normal.cn: 同一个「第一」词根出现在蛋白质、主角与原型中，都出自希腊语。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered seat that decides which row the whole theatre belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带编号的座位，它决定整个剧场属于哪一排。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp at the centre of a dark hall, giving light but never taking it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅中央的一盏灯，只给光，不取光。

abstract.en: Picture the first brick laid, whose position names the wall that follows.
abstract.cn: 想象砌下的第一块砖，它的位置为后面整堵墙命名。

examples.en: The nucleus of carbon holds six protons and six neutrons.
examples.cn: 碳的原子核含六个质子与六个中子。

examples.en: Chemists describe an acid as a proton donor.
examples.cn: 化学家把酸描述为质子供体。

examples.en: The sun burns by turning protons into helium.
examples.cn: 太阳靠把质子变成氦来发光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（在前）+ ton（吨）」——最前面那块最重的砖，就是质子

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」+ 粒子命名惯用的词尾；prōtos 更早的来源不明。英语形式即本词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the charged core of the atom, move to the bare hydrogen nucleus and the element count, then follow the same particle into acids, hospitals, cosmic rays, the solar wind and finally the sun's fusion chain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从原子带正电的核心出发，转到单独的氢核与元素编号，再让同一个粒子依次进入酸、医院、宇宙射线、太阳风，最后进入太阳的聚变链。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one positively charged brick at the centre of every atom, and the same brick alone in the simplest atom.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个原子中心一块带正电的砖，而在最简单的原子里只有这一块砖。

branches.en: ONE BRICK: whether inside a heavy nucleus or alone as hydrogen, the same charged brick is being named.
branches.cn: 同一块砖：无论在重核内部还是单独作为氢，被命名的都是这块带正电的砖。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: the count of bricks is written down as the name of the element.
branches.cn: 账本：砖的数目被记成元素的名称。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: chemistry treats the brick as a token that an acid gives away.
branches.cn: 交出：化学把这颗砖当作酸可以递出去的凭物。

branches.en: THE TRAVELLER: the same brick is aimed at a tumour, arrives from space, or streams out of the sun.
branches.cn: 远行者：同一颗砖或被瞄准肿瘤，或从太空抵达，或从太阳流出。

branches.en: THE FURNACE: in stars the brick becomes fuel, and four of them must meet to make helium.
branches.cn: 熔炉：在恒星里这砖成了燃料，四颗相会才能造出氦。

intro.en: Proton is a Greek noun, but its first-root and its particle ending both recur across scientific and everyday English.
intro.cn: 质子是希腊语名词，但它的「第一」词根与粒子结尾在科学与日常英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate of proton; the Latin word for first, primus, belongs to another family. The Greek forms below are the true parts.
latinIntro.cn: 质子没有拉丁同族词；拉丁语里表示「第一」的 primus 属于另一个词族。真正的构件是下面的希腊语形式。

items.example: The prefix marks whatever comes first in a series.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出系列中最先出现的那一个。

items.example: The adjective ranks one item ahead of all others.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把某一项排在所有其他项之前。

items.example: The proton sits at the centre of the atom.
The protonic charge balances the electron cloud.
items.exampleCN: 质子的电荷与电子云相抵。

items.meaning: to add a proton to a molecule
items.example: The acid protonates the base within microseconds.
items.exampleCN: 酸在微秒之内就使碱质子化。

items.meaning: a primary substance of living tissue
items.meaningCN: 生命组织里的首要成分
items.example: Protein was named as the first substance of the body.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质曾被命名为身体的首要物质。

items.example: The protagonist speaks first in every act.
items.exampleCN: 主角在每一幕里都最先开口。

items.meaning: the first model of a device
items.example: The prototype was tested before any copies were made.
items.exampleCN: 原型在任何复制品造出之前先接受了测试。

definition_zh: 为测试设计而造出的第一个完整模型或样机；也指某类事物的早期范例
definition_en: the first full working model of a design, built for testing, or an early example that a later type follows
core_image: 工作台上，一台用螺栓临时拼起的样机正在空转，外壳未喷漆，线束裸露，却已能完成主要动作
scene: 工作台上，一台用螺栓临时拼起的样机正在空转，外壳还没喷漆，线束露在外面。They built a prototype of the pump in a single week.
sceneCN: 这里指用于测试的样机（第 1 个义项：为测试设计而造出的第一个完整模型或样机）；句意：他们用一周时间造出了泵的样机。

pos.zh: 原型；样机；范例

derivatives.zh: 由「原型」加形容词词尾构成，义为「典型的、原型的」
由「典型的」加副词词尾构成，义为「典型地」
由「做原型」加动名词词尾构成，义为「原型制作」
由希腊语「最初的」与「印模」构成，义为「典范、原型」

senses.title: The first working model
senses.definition: the first complete model of a product, built so that its design can be tested
senses.definitionCN: 为测试设计而造出的产品第一个完整模型
senses.example: The prototype ran for ten minutes before the seal failed.
senses.exampleCN: 样机运行了十分钟后密封失效。
senses.why: Proto- means first and type means model, so the word is the first model of a kind.
senses.whyCN: 「第一」与「印模」相加，这个词就是同类中的第一个模型。

senses.title: A pre-production sample
senses.definition: a sample made with production methods to check tooling and assembly before mass output
senses.definitionCN: 用生产方式做出、在批量产出前检查工装与装配的样品
senses.example: The factory built ten prototypes before releasing the moulds.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂在开模之前造了十件试制样品。
senses.why: As a design approaches production, the first model becomes a sample that tests the factory, not only the idea.
senses.whyCN: 当设计接近生产时，第一个模型就变成检验工厂而不只检验想法的样品。

senses.title: A clickable software model
senses.definition: an interactive mock-up of screens used to test a workflow before code is written
senses.definitionCN: 在写代码之前用来测试流程的屏幕交互模型
senses.example: The team tested the checkout prototype with five users.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用五名用户测试了结账流程原型。
senses.why: Software has no metal to bend, so its first model is a set of linked screens.
senses.whyCN: 软件没有可弯的金属，因此它的第一个模型是一组相连的屏幕。

senses.title: A concept vehicle
senses.definition: a one-off vehicle built to show a design direction rather than to be sold
senses.definitionCN: 为展示设计方向而非出售而造的单台车辆
senses.example: The concept prototype had no door handles at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这台概念样车完全没有门把手。
senses.why: Transport design uses a full-size model to judge proportion, and that model is a prototype.
senses.whyCN: 交通工具设计用全尺寸模型判断比例，这个模型就是原型。

senses.title: A flight test article
senses.definition: an aircraft or engine built for flight testing before a production standard is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 在确定生产标准之前为飞行试验而造的飞机或发动机
senses.example: The first flight prototype carried extra sensors instead of seats.
senses.exampleCN: 第一架飞行样机装的是额外传感器而不是座椅。
senses.why: Flight cannot be simulated fully, so aviation builds a prototype that is meant to be flown and measured.
senses.whyCN: 飞行无法完全模拟，因此航空会造一架用于飞行与测量的原型。

senses.title: An early example of a type
senses.definition: a person or thing that later examples are modelled on
senses.definitionCN: 后来同类事物据以塑造的早期人或物
senses.example: The village is a prototype of the new eco-settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄是新生态聚落的原型。
senses.why: From first model comes the wider sense of a pattern that later things copy.
senses.whyCN: 从「第一个模型」引申出更宽的「后来者仿效的范式」之义。

senses.title: The best example of a category
senses.definition: the member of a category that most people regard as most typical of it
senses.definitionCN: 一个范畴中最被大众视为典型的那一个成员
senses.example: In prototype theory, a robin is a better prototype than an ostrich.
senses.exampleCN: 在原型理论中，知更鸟比鸵鸟更像典型样本。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for the mental best example that organizes a category.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词指组织范畴的心理最佳样本。

senses.title: A rough first version
senses.definition: any preliminary version of a document, plan or product made for comment
senses.definitionCN: 为征求意见而做的最初版本文件、方案或产品
senses.example: This report is only a prototype; the numbers will change.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告只是初版，数字还会变。
senses.why: Any first attempt can be called a prototype because it is made to be tested and replaced.
senses.whyCN: 任何第一次尝试都可称原型，因为它本来就是用来试验并替换的。

intro.en: Prototype joins two Greek elements, first and impression, and reached English through Latin; the modern industrial sense grew from the idea of an original impression.
intro.cn: 「原型」把两个希腊语成分「第一」与「印模」组合，经拉丁语进入英语；现代工业义从「最初的印痕」这一观念发展而来。

items.en: Protos meant first or foremost, and it begins many English words about priority.
items.cn: 这个希腊语词指第一或最前，它是许多表示优先的英语词的开头。

items.en: Typos meant a blow, the mark left by a blow, and so a model or impression; it is the source of English type.
items.cn: 这个希腊语名词指击打、击打留下的痕记，因此也指模子或印痕；它是英语「类型」的来源。

items.en: The compound meant an original model or first impression, the pattern from which copies are made.
items.cn: 这个复合词指最初的模子或第一次印痕，即据以复制出副本的范式。

items.en: Late Latin took the Greek compound as prototypum, keeping the sense of an original form.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把这个希腊复合词接收为「最初的模子」，保留了「原初形式」之义。

items.en: English used prototype from the sixteenth century for an original or a model, often in learned and religious writing.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起用这个词指原初之物或模子，多见于学术与宗教写作。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering narrowed the word to the first full model of a product, built to be tested before production.
items.cn: 二十世纪工程把词义缩小为产品的第一个完整模型，为生产前的测试而造。

note.en: The first group shares the type root; the second group names nearby model words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「印模」词根；第二组是相邻的模型用语。

entries.definition: A kind or a printed character; the root word behind prototype.
entries.definitionCN: 种类或印刷字符；原型背后的词根词。

entries.definition: Most typical of a category; derived from the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 某范畴中最典型的；由同一个词派生。

entries.definition: An original pattern or ideal model; it stresses origin more than testing.
entries.definitionCN: 原初范式或理想模型；强调起源而非测试。

entries.definition: A fixed oversimplified image; it shares the impression element.
entries.definitionCN: 固定而简化的印象；共享「印痕」成分。

entries.definition: A full-size model for appearance or layout, often not working.
entries.definitionCN: 用于看外观或布局的全尺寸模型，常不能运转。

entries.definition: One item taken to represent a batch; it need not be the first model.
entries.definitionCN: 从一批中取出代表整体的一个；不必是第一个模型。

entries.definition: A small trial production or plant before full scale; it stresses scale-up, not the first model.
entries.definitionCN: 全面推广前的小规模试产或试验厂；强调放大，而非第一个模型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: First plus impression equals the first model of a kind.
normal.cn: 「第一」加「印模」，等于同类中的第一个模型。

normal.en: The family runs prototype, prototypical, prototyping, archetype, stereotype.
normal.cn: 同族词包括原型、典型的、原型制作、原初范式、刻板印象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: working prototype, prototype stage, prototype testing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：可运行样机、原型阶段、样机测试。

normal.en: A prototype is built to be broken, measured and replaced.
normal.cn: 原型本来就是用来被弄坏、被测量并替换的。

normal.en: It differs from a mock-up by working, and from a sample by being first.
normal.cn: 它与模型样板的差别在于能运转，与样品的差别在于它是第一个。

abstract.en: Picture a rough clay figure made only to see whether the pose works.
abstract.cn: 想象一个粗捏的泥人，只为看看姿势是否成立。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut from soft wax before the metal is touched.
abstract.cn: 想象在碰金属之前先用软蜡削出一把钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a first draft written in pencil so that it can be erased without regret.
abstract.cn: 想象一份用铅笔写的初稿，擦掉也不心疼。

examples.en: The prototype leaked, so the seal was redesigned.
examples.cn: 样机漏了，于是密封被重新设计。

examples.en: A prototype is judged by what it teaches, not by how it looks.
examples.cn: 样机的价值在于它教给我们什么，而不在于它好不好看。

examples.en: The museum keeps the prototype of the first electric kettle.
examples.cn: 博物馆保存着第一只电水壶的原型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「第一」个「印模」——先压出一个样子，再照着做

root: 由希腊语「第一」与「击打留下的印痕、模子」复合，经晚期拉丁语进入英语；现代工业义为生产前测试的第一个完整模型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one first model: it is built, tested, shown, flown, copied and finally treated as the type of its kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随一个最初的模型：它被造出、被测试、被展示、被飞行、被仿效，最后被视为同类之型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough first build standing on a bench, wires showing, made only to be tested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台粗糙的初版样机立在台面上，线束外露，生来就是为了被测试。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL FIRST: a working model and a pre-production sample.
branches.cn: 实体初版：可工作的模型与量产前样品。

branches.en: THE SOFTWARE VERSION: linked screens instead of metal.
branches.cn: 软件版本：相连的屏幕而非金属。

branches.en: THE TRANSPORT VERSION: concept vehicles and flight test articles.
branches.cn: 交通版本：概念样车与飞行试验样机。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE VERSION: an early pattern, and the best member of a category.
branches.cn: 范例版本：早期范式与范畴中的最佳样本。

branches.en: THE DRAFT VERSION: any rough first version offered for comment.
branches.cn: 草案版本：任何供征求意见的粗略初版。

intro.en: Both elements are Greek: first, and the mark left by a blow that became the word for type.
intro.cn: 两个成分都是希腊语：表示「第一」的词，以及击打留下的痕记，后者成为「类型」一词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin prototypum carried the Greek compound into European use.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语的「最初模子」把这个希腊复合词带入欧洲语言。

items.meaning: a blow; the mark left; a model

items.exampleCN: 它与目标词并列构成「原初范式」。

typus, typi (n., second declension, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: 由「原型」加形容词词尾构成，义为「典型的」
由「典型的」加副词词尾构成，义为「典型地」
由「做原型」加动名词词尾构成，义为「原型制作」
由希腊语「最初」与「模子」构成，义为「原初范式」
