definition_zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验；证明自己
definition_en: to show that something is true by evidence, to turn out to be a particular way, or to test something in practice
core_image: 一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停了下来
scene: 争论一直持续到深夜，直到有人把当年的登记簿翻到那一页，指着上面的签名。The old register proved that the land had belonged to her family.
sceneCN: 这里表示「证明、证实」（第 1 个义项：用证据使某件事确定为真）；句意为那本旧登记簿证明了这块地一直属于她家。

pos.zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验

derivatives.zh: 与 prove 同源的名词，经古法语 preove 而来，义为「证据；证明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被证实的；经考验的」
由 prove 加 -able 构成，义为「可证明的」
由 prove 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「证明……有误；驳倒」

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to give facts, documents or tests that make it certain that something is true or real
senses.definitionCN: 拿出事实、文件或检验，使某事被确定为真或确实存在
senses.example: The fingerprints proved that he had been in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹证明他曾在那间屋子里。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test something and find it good, so proving starts as an examination that ends in a verdict rather than as a mere opinion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验某物并认定它站得住，所以「证明」起初是一场检验，最后落成判决，而不只是看法。

senses.title: To turn out to be a particular thing
senses.definition: to be found, after events have unfolded, to have a certain quality, often one that was not expected
senses.definitionCN: 事情展开之后，被发现具有某种性质，且常是原先没料到的
senses.example: The shortcut proved longer than the road we usually take.
senses.exampleCN: 那条近路结果比我们常走的路还远。
senses.why: Once a test is finished, the result simply is what it is; English lets the verb carry that outcome, so a thing can prove difficult without anyone proving it.
senses.whyCN: 检验结束之后，结果就摆在那里；英语让这个动词直接承担结果，于是事物本身可以 prove difficult，而不需要谁去证明它。

senses.title: To test something in order to learn its quality
senses.definition: to try a method, a weapon or a machine under real conditions to see whether it works
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下试用某种方法、武器或机器，看它是否管用
senses.example: The engineers proved the new pump under heavy load before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在重载下检验了新水泵，然后才出售。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer made visible: before a thing can be proved true, it has to be put to the test, and the verb still names that trial.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老那层意思的直接显现：在被证明为真之前，东西得先经受检验，而这个动词至今仍指那场试验。

senses.title: To show one's own ability or courage
senses.definition: to show through action that one deserves a place, a role or respect
senses.definitionCN: 通过行动表明自己配得上某个位置、角色或尊重
senses.example: She proved herself in her first month on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她在上夜班的第一个月就证明了自己。
senses.why: When the thing being proved is the speaker, the test and the result collapse into one act, which is why English says prove oneself rather than adding true as well.
senses.whyCN: 当被证明的对象是说话者本人时，检验与结果合成一个动作，所以英语说 prove oneself，不再额外加 true。

intro.en: Prove descends from a Latin verb that meant to test and to judge as good; English keeps both the trial and the verdict, and later let the word also mean to turn out.
intro.cn: prove 源自一个意为「检验并判定为好」的拉丁动词；英语同时保留了检验与判决，后来又让它表示「结果如何」。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest and of good quality, said of a person or a thing that had been checked.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、品质良好，用于经过查验的人或物。

items.en: Probare meant to test something and to approve it as good, joining the act of examining to the verdict.
items.cn: probare 意为检验某物并认可它合格，把查验的动作与判决连在一起。

items.en: The participle probatus described what had stood the test, and it is the shape behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词 probatus 描述经住了检验的东西，是英语这个词背后的形式。

items.en: Old French prover meant to test and to demonstrate, and it brought the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 prover 意为检验、论证，把这个动词带进英语。

items.en: English split the old family: proof became the noun for the evidence, while prove kept the testing and added the modern sense of turning out.
items.cn: 英语把这一族拆开：proof 成为表示证据的名词，prove 留住检验，又添上「结果是」这层现代用法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of testing, including the noun English split off from it; the second group gathers verbs for showing something to be true or false.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「检验」的拉丁动词，包括英语从它分出去的名词；第二组收表示「表明真假」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for evidence that settles a question, split off from the same French form.
entries.definitionCN: 能定下疑问的证据名词，与动词同出法语形式。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something already shown to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作形容词，指已被证实的东西。

entries.definition: Likely to be true, from the same Latin verb of testing and approving.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的，出自同一个表示检验与认可的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To investigate closely, originally to test a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查究，原指探查伤口或表面。

entries.definition: To show clearly by argument or by an example.
entries.definitionCN: 用论证或实例清楚地表明。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实、准确。

entries.definition: To show that a fact is certain, often in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事实确凿，常较正式。

entries.definition: To be discovered to be a particular way in the end.
entries.definitionCN: 最终被发现是某种样子。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps the picture of a test that ends in a verdict: something is put under pressure, and the result is then allowed to speak.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词保留着「检验之后落成判决」的画面：某物被压上压力，然后让结果自己说话。

normal.en: Probare is to test and to approve, so prove carries a courtroom inside it: first the examination, then the finding.
normal.cn: probare 既是检验也是认可，所以 prove 里装着一间法庭：先审，再判。

normal.en: Proof is the same family seen as a thing rather than an act, which is why a proof is handed over while a prove is performed.
normal.cn: proof 是同一族词被看成「物」而不是「动作」，所以 proof 可以递过去，prove 只能被执行。

normal.en: Probable keeps the approving half: what is probable has enough testing behind it to be believed.
normal.cn: probable 保留了「认可」的那一半：很可能的事，背后已有足够的检验让人相信。

normal.en: Disprove adds dis- to the front, so the test now ends in rejection instead of approval.
normal.cn: disprove 在前面加 dis-，于是检验以否定而不是认可收场。

normal.en: Prove looks like protect because both start with pro-, but probare means to test, and there is no covering anywhere in it.
normal.cn: prove 与 protect 都以 pro- 开头，但 probare 意为检验，其中没有任何「遮盖」。

abstract.en: A proof is a test that has stopped being a question, and the verb marks the moment that change happens.
abstract.cn: 证据是一场不再提问的检验，而这个动词标出的正是那变化发生的瞬间。

abstract.en: One word covers testing, judging and turning out because all three are stages of the same examination.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指检验、判定与结果，因为三者是同一场查验的不同阶段。

abstract.en: To prove something is to accept that it might fail, which is why the word is as much about risk as about certainty.
abstract.cn: 证明某物，就是承认它有可能失败，所以这个词既关乎确定，也关乎冒险。

examples.en: The video proved that the door had been locked all night.
examples.cn: 录像证明那扇门整夜都锁着。

examples.en: The task proved harder than anyone expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务结果比任何人预料的都难。

examples.en: He worked two extra shifts to prove himself.
examples.cn: 他多上了两个班来证明自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普如夫」——像「扑过去捋清楚」，把乱糟糟的事捋到只剩一条真相；记住 prove 是证明。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直的、品质良好的）→ probare（检验、验后认可）→ probatus（经住检验的），经古法语 prover 进入英语；同族词还有 proof、probable、probe、probity。注意 prove 与 protect 都带前缀 pro-，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），两者只是前缀相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a test ending in a verdict; the senses run from proving a fact, through the result of events, to testing a thing and proving oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以检验收尾的判定」；义项从证明一个事实，到事情的结果，再到检验一物与证明自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of papers pushed across a table, and a stamp on the last page that ends every doubt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停下来。

branches.en: a register opened to the page with the signature
branches.cn: 登记簿翻到有签名的那一页

branches.en: a short cut that turns out longer
branches.cn: 结果反而更远的那条近路

branches.en: a pump running under heavy load
branches.cn: 重载下运转的水泵

branches.en: a new worker taking the hardest shift
branches.cn: 新人接下最难的班次

branches.en: one word for examining and for concluding
branches.cn: 同一个词既指查验也指结论

intro.en: A Latin adjective of good quality, the verb of testing built on it, and the French and English forms that split into proof and prove hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示品质良好的拉丁形容词、由它构成的「检验」动词，以及分化为 proof 与 prove 的法语、英语形式，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Probus, probare and probatus are the reliable Latin cognates, and proof is the same family seen as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: probus、probare 与 probatus 是可靠的同源词；proof 则是同一族词被看成名词的样子。

definition_zh: 来源；出处；文物或艺术品的流传经历；动植物的原产地
definition_en: the origin or source of an object; the documented history of ownership of an artwork or artifact
core_image: 策展人摊开一叠旧拍卖目录与收据，把画作的每次转手按年份串起来
scene: 策展人翻看一叠旧拍卖目录，追查画作的流转。The painting's provenance can be traced to a Florentine collection.
sceneCN: 这里 provenance 指「艺术品历次转手与收藏的来源记录」（第 2 个义项：收藏流传史）；句意为这幅画的流传经历可追溯到一批佛罗伦萨旧藏。

pos.zh: 来源；出处；流传经历；原产地

derivatives.zh: provenance + -ed（形容词后缀）→ 有明确来源的
provenance 的变体 → 出处（考古学常用）
法语 provenir「来自」→ 源自（法语词）
拉丁 provenire「出来、起源」→ 出现；源自

senses.title: The origin or source of an object
senses.definition: the place, person or process from which an object came
senses.definitionCN: 物体来自的地点、人或过程
senses.example: The provenance of the stone is a quarry in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石头的来源是北方的一处采石场。
senses.why: provenir means 'to come forth', so provenance literally names where something came from.
senses.whyCN: provenir 意为「出来、源自」，因此 provenance 字面就指某物来自何处。

senses.title: The ownership history of an artwork
senses.definition: the documented sequence of owners and sales through which a work has passed
senses.definitionCN: 一件作品经历的所有者与交易的有记录序列
senses.example: The painting's provenance can be traced to a Florentine collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的流传经历可追溯到一批佛罗伦萨旧藏。
senses.why: owners and sales form a recorded sequence, so origin becomes ownership history.
senses.whyCN: 所有者与交易构成有记录的序列，因此「来源」变成「收藏史」。

senses.title: The native place of a plant or animal
senses.definition: the region where a species or variety naturally originated
senses.definitionCN: 某物种或品种自然起源的地区
senses.example: Botanists recorded the provenance of each seed lot.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家记录了每批种子的原产地。
senses.why: plants also come from somewhere, so the origin question applies to species.
senses.whyCN: 植物也来自某处，因此「来源」问题同样适用于物种。

senses.title: A documented chain of custody
senses.definition: the paper trail of receipts, catalogues and museum records that proves continuous possession
senses.definitionCN: 由收据、目录与博物馆记录构成的书面链条，证明连续持有
senses.example: Without a chain of custody, the provenance of the mask is incomplete.
senses.exampleCN: 没有保管链，这件面具的来源记录就不完整。
senses.why: receipts and records prove continuous possession, which is the custody sense.
senses.whyCN: 收据与记录证明连续持有，这就是「保管链」义。

senses.title: The find site of an artifact
senses.definition: the archaeological place where an object was recovered, recorded in site records
senses.definitionCN: 物件被发现的考古地点，记录在遗址档案中
senses.example: The provenance of the pot is a burial cave in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这件陶罐的出土地点是山中的一处墓葬洞穴。
senses.why: archaeology fixes origin to a recorded find spot.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把「来源」固定在一个有记录的出土地点。

senses.title: Evidence of authenticity
senses.definition: the provenance record used to argue that an object is genuine rather than forged
senses.definitionCN: 用来论证物件为真而非赝品的来源记录
senses.example: The auction house questioned the provenance before accepting the drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖行在接受这幅素描前质疑了它的来源证据。
senses.why: a documented trail is used as evidence that the object is not a forgery.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的链条被用作物件并非赝品的证据。

senses.title: The geographic source of a product
senses.definition: the region or country that a food, wine or material is said to come from
senses.definitionCN: 食品、葡萄酒或材料被宣称来自的地区或国家
senses.example: The label protects the provenance of the cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标签保护这种奶酪的原产地。
senses.why: food and wine law uses origin as a protected geographic claim.
senses.whyCN: 食品与葡萄酒法规把「来源」用作受保护的地理主张。

senses.title: The origin of a book copy
senses.definition: the earlier owners and collections of a particular printed copy
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定印本的早期所有者与收藏
senses.example: The library notes the provenance of each rare book on its catalogue card.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆在目录卡上注明每本善本的藏书来源。
senses.why: library catalogues record earlier owners, a narrow book-history use.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆目录记录早期所有者，是「书籍史」的窄用。

intro.en: Provenance comes from French provenance, from provenir 'to come forth', from Latin provenire, built on pro- 'forth' and venire 'to come'. The word names the coming-forth of an object rather than the object itself.
intro.cn: provenance 来自法语 provenance，源于 provenir「出来、源自」，再上溯拉丁 provenire，由 pro-「向前」与 venire「来」构成。这个词命名物件的「出来之处」，而非物件本身。

items.en: Venire meant 'to come', the base of many English words from invent to convene.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，是 invent 到 convene 等许多英语词的基础。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus venire gave provenire, 'to come forth, to originate'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 venire 构成 provenire，意为「出来、起源」。

items.en: French provenir kept the sense of coming from a source.
items.cn: 法语 provenir 保留「来自某处」的意思。

items.en: The noun provenance named the fact or place of origin, and English borrowed it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 名词 provenance 指来源这一事实或地点，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: Collectors and dealers narrowed the word to the documented ownership history of valuable objects.
items.cn: 收藏家与经销商把这个词收窄为贵重物件的书面收藏史。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest English use is dated differently across dictionaries, though the French and Latin chain is clear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各词典给出的英语首见年代不一，但法语与拉丁链条清楚。

note.en: Group one holds origin words easily confused with provenance; group two holds words for where a thing comes from.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 provenance 混淆的来源词；第二组是表示事物来处的词。

entries.definition: A variant spelling used in archaeology for the find site of an object; provenance is the standard art-market word.
entries.definitionCN: 考古学中用于出土地点的变体拼写；provenance 是艺术市场标准词。

entries.definition: An rare adjective meaning 'originating from'; it describes a source rather than records one.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见形容词，意为「源自」；它描述来源，而非记录来源。

entries.definition: Provisional or conditional; it sounds similar but belongs to a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 临时的或有条件的；发音相近，但属于不同词根。

entries.definition: The point where something begins; provenance adds documentation and ownership history.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始之处；provenance 增添了文献记录与收藏史。

entries.definition: The place or thing something comes from; it is broader and needs no paper trail.
entries.definitionCN: 事物来自的地点或东西；范围更广，不要求书面链条。

entries.definition: A recorded line of descent, used of animals, people or objects; provenance is the object's version.
entries.definitionCN: 有记录的世系，用于动物、人或物件；provenance 是物件版。

entries.definition: The whole past of a thing; provenance is the specific record of where and through whose hands it came.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的全部过去；provenance 是它来自何处、经过谁手的特定记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin coming verb, the French noun and the real auction paper trail.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「来」动词、法语名词与真实的拍卖文书链。

normal.en: pro- 'forth' plus venire 'come' gives 'come forth'.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 venire「来」构成「出来」。

normal.en: The same venire runs through invent, convene and advent.
normal.cn: 同一个 venire 贯穿 invent、convene 与 advent。

normal.en: Provenance is proved by receipts, catalogues and museum records.
normal.cn: 来源由收据、目录与博物馆记录证明。

normal.en: A clear provenance raises both value and authenticity.
normal.cn: 清晰的来源同时提升价值与真实性。

normal.en: Provenience is the archaeologist's variant for find site.
normal.cn: provenience 是考古学家指出土地点的变体。

abstract.en: Provenance is the paper shadow that follows an object through time.
abstract.cn: 来源是跟着物件穿越时间的纸质影子。

abstract.en: It is a chain of hands, written down.
abstract.cn: 它是一条被写下来的手手相传之链。

abstract.en: An object without provenance is a voice without a name.
abstract.cn: 没有来源的物件，是一个没有名字的声音。

examples.en: The museum published the provenance of every object in the show.
examples.cn: 博物馆公布了展览中每件物品的来源。

examples.en: The manuscript's provenance includes a monastery library.
examples.cn: 这份手稿的流传经历包括一座修道院图书馆。

examples.en: Scientists tested the provenance of the marble with isotope analysis.
examples.cn: 科学家用同位素分析检测大理石的原产地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ ven（来）」——从某处出来的 → 来源、出处

root: 法语 provenance ← provenir「出来、源自」← 拉丁 provenire「出来、起源」= pro-「向前」+ venire「来」。英语十七世纪借入，后收窄为艺术品与文物的流传来源记录。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a coming-forth: an object's source, an art work's owners, a plant's native range, a custody trail, a find site, proof of authenticity, a product's region and a book's earlier owners.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「出来之处」展开：物件来源、艺术品藏家、植物原产地、保管链、出土地点、真实性证明、产品产区与藏书旧主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of old receipts and catalogues tracing one object hand by hand back to its first home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠旧收据与目录，把一件物件一手接一手地追溯回最初的家。

branches.en: WHERE IT CAME FROM: an object's source and a plant's native range are the same origin question for different things.
branches.cn: 来自何处：物件来源与植物原产地是不同事物的同一来源问题。

branches.en: DOCUMENTED HANDS: ownership history and chain of custody are the same paper trail at narrative and evidential levels.
branches.cn: 有记录的手：收藏史与保管链是同一纸质链条的叙述面与证据面。

branches.en: FIND SITE: archaeology fixes the coming-forth to a place in the ground.
branches.cn: 出土地点：考古学把「出来之处」固定在土地中的某一点。

branches.en: PROOF: a clean trail becomes evidence that the object is genuine.
branches.cn: 证明：干净的链条成为物件为真的证据。

branches.en: PLACE AND BOOK: a product's region and a copy's earlier owners are two narrower uses of the same origin record.
branches.cn: 产地与藏书：产品产区与印本旧主是同一来源记录的两种窄用。

intro.en: Provenance is a French noun on a Latin verb, and its root also builds a large family of coming words.
intro.cn: provenance 是建立在拉丁动词之上的法语名词，其词根还构成一大串表示「来」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire gives invent, convene, advent and event; pro- adds the direction 'forth'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire 衍生 invent、convene、advent 与 event；pro- 增添「向前」方向。

items.structure: venire, veni, ventum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀增添向外方向。

items.structure: provenire, proveni, proventum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)

derivatives.zh: provenance + -ed（形容词后缀）→ 有明确来源的
provenance 的变体 → 出土地点（考古学）
法语 provenir「来自」→ 源自（法语词）
拉丁 provenire「出来、起源」→ 出现；源自

definition_zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；防备
definition_en: to give or supply something that is needed, to state a rule in a law or contract, or to support someone with money
core_image: 旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，再转身把干粮和水递给身后的人
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，村口的空地上支起几张长桌，志愿者把水和面包摆成一排。The relief team came to provide blankets and hot food for the flooded villages.
sceneCN: 这里取「提供、供给」的意思（第 1 个义项：把别人需要的东西给出去）；句意为救援队来为受淹的村庄提供毛毯和热食。村口长桌上摆开的水和面包就是线索。

pos.zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；为…做准备

derivatives.zh: 由 provide 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「供应者；提供者」
由拉丁语名词 provisio（预见、照料）经法语进入英语，义为「供应；条款；储备」
由拉丁词干 provid- 加 -ent 构成，义为「有远见的；用钱谨慎的」
由过去分词转成的连词，义为「假如；只要」，常见于 provided that

senses.title: To supply something that is needed
senses.definition: to give someone something they need or to make something available for use
senses.definitionCN: 把别人需要的东西给出去，或使某物可供使用
senses.example: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。
senses.why: Latin providere joins pro-, ahead, to videre, to see; seeing ahead means noticing a need before it arrives, and the next move is to get the thing ready and hand it over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 providere 把表示「在前」的 pro- 接在 videre（看）上：提前看见，就是在需求到来之前先察觉；察觉之后最自然的动作，就是把东西备好递过去，于是「预先看见」变成了「供给」。

senses.title: To state as a rule in a law or contract
senses.definition: to establish a rule or condition in a law, contract or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、合同或协议中确立某条规则或条件
senses.example: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。
senses.why: A rule written in advance is itself a kind of foresight: the text settles now what will happen later, so the verb that means to get ready also names what a document lays down beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 提前写好的条文本身就是一种预见：文本在此刻就决定了以后会发生什么，所以那个表示「预先备好」的动词，也用来指文件事先订下的内容。

senses.title: To support someone financially
senses.definition: to earn the money that allows another person, especially a family member, to live
senses.definitionCN: 挣钱供另一个人生活，尤指供养家庭成员
senses.example: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。
senses.why: Providing for someone is looking ahead on their behalf: the money is set aside before the need is felt, which is the household version of seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 供养一个人，就是替对方往前看：钱在需求出现之前就留出来，这正是「预先看见」在家庭里的样子。

senses.title: To make preparation against something
senses.definition: to take action in advance so that a possible problem or danger does less harm
senses.definitionCN: 提前采取行动，使可能出现的问题或危险危害更小
senses.example: They built the wall to provide against flooding in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了这道墙，用来防备春季洪水。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure foresight with nothing given away: to provide against a risk is to see it coming and move before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是纯粹的「预先看见」，与给东西无关：provide against 某个风险，就是看出它会来，并在它落地之前先动手。

intro.en: Provide is built from two Latin pieces meaning ahead and to see, and that single image of foresight later spreads into supply, legal rules and family support.
intro.cn: provide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，意思分别是「在前」和「看」；这一「预先看见」的画面后来扩展到供给、法律条文与养家。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it supplied the visual core of a large family of Latin words.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，为一大族拉丁词提供了「看」这个核心。

items.en: Pro- meant ahead or in front, so providere meant to see ahead, to foresee and to take care of something in advance.
items.cn: pro- 表示「在前、预先」，所以 providere 意为往前看、预见，并提前照管某事。

items.en: The noun providentia named foresight and careful management, and it survives in the English words providence and provident.
items.cn: 名词 providentia 指远见与谨慎的照料，它留在英语的 providence 与 provident 里。

items.en: Old French pourveoir kept both halves of the meaning: to foresee a need and to supply what it calls for.
items.cn: 古法语 pourveoir 保留了两半意思：既预见需求，也提供需求所需的东西。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as provide and carried the word into law, where a document provides, and into the household, where a wage provides for a family.
items.cn: 英语把拼写固定为 provide，并把这个词带进法律——文件可以「规定」，也带进家庭——工资可以「养家」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving what is needed.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示「给出所需之物」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for supplying something, and also a clause in a document.
entries.definitionCN: 表示供应之事的名字，也指文件中的条款。

entries.definition: Care or guidance that looks ahead, often attributed to a higher power.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来作准备的照管，常被归于更高的力量。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A person or a company that supplies something.
entries.definitionCN: 提供某物的人或机构。

entries.definition: To give or sell what is needed over time.
entries.definitionCN: 持续提供或出售所需之物。

entries.definition: To provide furniture or whatever else is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 提供家具或所需之物。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to take.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西拿出来供人取用。

entries.definition: To supply with tools or skills for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的提供工具或技能。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a look into the future, not with a gift, and its family keeps returning to foresight, readiness and the handover that follows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是送礼；同族词反复回到预见、准备以及随之而来的交付。

normal.en: Pro- means ahead and videre means to see, so provide begins with a look into the future rather than with an object.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前」，videre 意为「看」，所以 provide 的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是某件东西。

normal.en: Provision is the noun built on the same stem: what has been seen ahead and therefore got ready.
normal.cn: provision 是同一词干上的名词：预先看见、因此备好的东西。

normal.en: The legal use, as in the law provides, works because a written rule also decides the future in advance.
normal.cn: 法律用法如 the law provides 之所以成立，是因为写下的规则同样在提前决定未来。

normal.en: Provider adds -er, the person who does the providing, exactly as in employer and adviser.
normal.cn: provider 加 -er，指做「提供」这件事的人，与 employer、adviser 的构造相同。

normal.en: Provided that keeps the past participle and turns it into a condition: if this is seen to, the rest follows.
normal.cn: provided that 保留过去分词形式，把它变成条件：只要这一点被照看到，其余便随之成立。

abstract.en: To provide is to act on a future you have already seen, which is why the word sounds like care more than charity.
abstract.cn: 提供是对一个你已经看见的未来采取行动，所以这个词听起来更像照料，而不像施舍。

abstract.en: A law that provides and a parent who provides are doing one thing: fixing tomorrow before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 法律规定与父母供养做的是同一件事：在明天到来之前就把它安排下来。

abstract.en: The whole word lives in the gap between seeing a need and meeting it.
abstract.cn: 从看见需求到满足需求之间的那段距离，正是这个词的全部所在。

examples.en: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。

examples.en: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。

examples.en: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
examples.cn: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若外德」——听着像「铺好喂的」，先把吃的用的铺好喂到人跟前，正是提供。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前、预先）+ videre（看见）构成 providere，本义「预先看到、提前照管」，由此引申为「预备、供给、规定、供养」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight; the senses divide into supplying a need, writing a rule down, supporting a family, and guarding against a risk.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预先看见」；义项分成满足需求、把规则写下来、供养家人，以及防备风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller standing on a rise, looking far down the road, then turning back to hand food and water to those behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，然后转身把干粮和水递给身后的人。

branches.en: a table of food laid out before anyone asks
branches.cn: 没人开口前就摆好的一桌食物

branches.en: a clause printed in small type at the end of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾用小字印出的条款

branches.en: a wage that keeps an old couple fed
branches.cn: 让一对老人吃得上饭的一份工资

branches.en: a wall raised before the river rises
branches.cn: 河水上涨之前就砌起的墙

branches.en: a store of grain kept for a bad year
branches.cn: 为荒年留下的存粮

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of seeing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示「看见」的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, the compound providere, to see ahead, and the noun providentia, foresight, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、复合形式 providere（往前看）与名词 providentia（远见）是英语这个词的直接来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to see ahead, to take care

definition_zh: 条款；规定；供应；提供；储备；预备
definition_en: a condition written into a law or contract, the act of supplying something, or a store of supplies kept for future use
core_image: 仓库里一袋袋粮食靠墙码好，门边贴着一张写明分配办法的纸
scene: 出发去山区之前，队长把面粉和罐头清点了一遍，又把分配办法写在纸上贴到门边。The expedition carried enough provisions for two weeks in the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里取「储备、给养」的意思（第 3 个义项：为将来备下的物资）；句意为探险队带上了足够在山里用两周的给养。靠墙码好的粮食和罐头就是线索。

pos.zh: 条款；规定；供应；提供；储备；预备

collocations.phrase: under the provisions of the law

derivatives.zh: 与 provision 同出拉丁语 providere（预先看见），义为「提供；规定」
由 provision 加 -al 构成，义为「临时的；暂定的」
由 provisional 加 -ly 构成，义为「暂时地；暂定地」

senses.title: A condition written into a law or contract
senses.definition: a condition or clause in a law, contract or agreement that states what must be done
senses.definitionCN: 法律、合同或协议中写明必须如何做的条件或条款
senses.example: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。
senses.why: Latin provisio meant a seeing ahead, and a clause is exactly foresight written down: the parties decide now what will happen if something goes wrong later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provisio 意为「预先看见」，而条款正是被写下来的预见：各方在此刻就定好，以后出了某种情况该怎么办。

senses.title: The act of supplying something
senses.definition: the act of giving or supplying something, especially a service or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予或供应某物的行为，尤指服务或资源
senses.example: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
senses.exampleCN: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。
senses.why: Once foresight turns into action, the action is supplying, and English uses the noun for the whole process of making something available.
senses.whyCN: 预见一旦化为行动，这个行动就是供应；英语用这个名词指「使某物可供使用」的整个过程。

senses.title: A store of supplies kept for future use
senses.definition: supplies of food, fuel or equipment kept ready, especially for a journey or an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 备好的食物、燃料或装备，尤指为旅途或应急准备的
senses.example: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。
senses.why: What foresight produces is something set aside, so the noun shifts from the act of preparing to the goods sitting in the store room, usually in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 预见所产生的，就是被留出来的东西，于是这个名词从「准备的动作」转到「仓库里堆着的物资」，且常用复数。

senses.title: Preparation made in advance
senses.definition: arrangements made now so that a future need or risk is already taken care of
senses.definitionCN: 现在作出的安排，使将来的需求或风险已被照管到
senses.example: They made provision for their daughter's education years in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们多年前就为女儿的教育作了准备。
senses.why: This is the word at its closest to the Latin original: pure forethought, before anything has been handed over or stored.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最贴近拉丁原义的一层：纯粹的预先打算，还没有交出任何东西，也还没有囤起任何东西。

intro.en: Provision comes from a Latin noun of foresight built on the same verb as provide, and English borrowed the noun through French.
intro.cn: provision 来自一个表示「预见」的拉丁语名词，与 provide 建立在同一个动词上；英语是经法语借入这个名词的。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the plain visual root behind the whole family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，是整族词背后那个朴素的「看」的词根。

items.en: Providere meant to see ahead and to take care in advance, with pro- adding the forward direction.
items.cn: providere 意为往前看、提前照料，前缀 pro- 加上了「向前」的方向。

items.en: The noun provisio named the act of foreseeing and the care that followed from it; its stem provis- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 provisio 指预见这一动作以及随之而来的照料，英语保留的正是它的词干 provis-。

items.en: Old French provision carried the noun into the senses of supply and of a stipulated arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语 provision 把这个名词带到「供应」与「约定好的安排」这两层意思上。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for a clause or the act of supplying, and the plural for goods stored up for a journey.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指条款或供应的行为，用复数指为旅途囤起来的物资。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers words for clauses and for what is kept in store.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示条款与囤积之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to supply or to stipulate.
entries.definitionCN: 表示提供或规定的动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for the present only, to be changed later.
entries.definitionCN: 只为眼前安排的，以后会更改的。

entries.definition: Foresight and care, often seen as guidance from above.
entries.definitionCN: 远见与照料，常被视为来自上方的指引。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A single condition in a legal document.
entries.definitionCN: 法律文件中的单项条件。

entries.definition: An amount of something available for use.
entries.definitionCN: 可供使用的某物数量。

entries.definition: Goods kept in store for future use.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来使用而存着的货物。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met in an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 协议中必须满足的条件。

normalIntro.en: The word is foresight that has cooled into an object, and its memories sit on the Latin stem, on the written clause and on the plural in the store room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是冷却成实物的预见，记忆点落在拉丁词干、写下的条款，以及仓库里的复数形式上。

normal.en: Provision and provide share the Latin verb providere, but the noun came through French while the verb came by another route, which is why the vowel changed.
normal.cn: provision 与 provide 共享拉丁语动词 providere，但名词经法语传来，动词走的是另一条路，所以元音变了。

normal.en: Provis- is the stem of Latin provisio, so the -sion ending was not added in English.
normal.cn: provis- 是拉丁语 provisio 的词干，所以 -sion 并不是英语后来加上的后缀。

normal.en: Provisional keeps the idea of something arranged in advance and adds the hint that the arrangement is only for now.
normal.cn: provisional 保留「事先安排」的意思，并加上「这个安排只管眼前」的意味。

normal.en: In contracts the word means a clause, because a clause is a piece of written foresight.
normal.cn: 在合同里这个词指条款，因为条款就是一段写下来的预见。

normal.en: The plural provisions almost always means food and equipment for a journey, not several clauses.
normal.cn: 复数 provisions 几乎总指旅途所需的食物和装备，而不是好几条条款。

abstract.en: Provision is foresight that has cooled into an object: a clause on paper or a sack in the store room.
abstract.cn: provision 是冷却成实物的预见：要么是纸上的一条条款，要么是仓库里的一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Every contract is a small machine for the future, and its provisions are the parts.
abstract.cn: 每份合同都是一台为未来造的小机器，条款就是它的零件。

abstract.en: To make provision is to admit that the future will ask for something you do not yet need.
abstract.cn: 作出准备，就是承认未来会来索要你此刻还不需要的东西。

examples.en: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
examples.cn: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。

examples.en: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
examples.cn: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。

examples.en: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
examples.cn: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若维仁」——听着像「铺若为仁」，先替别人把东西铺好，正是供应与储备。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight turning into arrangement; the senses divide into the written clause, the act of supplying, the goods stored up, and preparation made in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预见变成安排」；义项分成写下的条款、供应的行为、囤起来的物资，以及提前作出的准备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks stacked against a store room wall, with a sheet of paper beside the door setting out how they will be shared.

branches.en: a clause printed in small type
branches.cn: 用小字印出的一条条款

branches.en: a pipe carrying water into a district
branches.cn: 把水送进街区的一根管道

branches.en: sacks stacked against a store room wall
branches.cn: 靠着仓库墙码起的口袋

branches.cn: 一份条约以及条约里承诺的粮食

intro.en: A Latin verb of seeing ahead and the noun built from it hold the word together, and French passed the noun on with its stem intact.
intro.cn: 表示「预先看见」的拉丁语动词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，法语连词干一起把它传了下来。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, providere, to see ahead, and the noun provisio, a foreseeing, are the direct sources of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、providere（往前看）与名词 provisio（预见）是英语这个名词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起；煽动
definition_en: to stir someone into anger or action, or to cause a reaction or an event
core_image: 有人把一根长杆伸进静止的水面，圈圈波纹从杆尖向外荡开
scene: 这份提案把两边的旧账都翻了出来，会上争了两个小时。The proposal provoked a long debate in the council.
sceneCN: 这里指引起一场争论（第 3 个义项：引发反应或讨论）；句意为这份提案在议会引发了长时间辩论。图中可辨识物件：伸进水面的长杆、向外荡开的波纹、静止的水；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅；激怒；诱因」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的；引人深思的」

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to stir a person into anger, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 使某人动怒，常带故意成分
senses.example: His remarks provoked the crowd outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话激怒了厅外的人群。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to call forth, and anger is one of the things called out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「唤出」，而怒气正是从人身上被唤出来的东西之一。

senses.title: To challenge deliberately
senses.definition: to invite a fight or a strong reaction by confronting someone on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意顶撞某人，以招来争斗或强烈反应
senses.example: The guard was provoked into opening the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门卫被激得打开了大门。
senses.why: Provocation is a call the other person is expected to answer, which is why it feels like an invitation.
senses.whyCN: 挑衅是一声预期对方会回应的召唤，所以才像一份邀请。

senses.title: To give rise to a reaction
senses.definition: to cause a response, discussion or public reaction without any intent to anger
senses.definitionCN: 引起回应、讨论或公众反应，不含激怒意图
senses.example: The report provoked wide discussion in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在报界引发广泛讨论。
senses.why: The oldest neutral sense simply calls a response into being, with no emotional charge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的中性义只是把回应唤出来，不带情绪色彩。

senses.title: To arouse interest
senses.definition: to make curiosity or interest appear in someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生好奇或兴趣
senses.example: The strange photograph provoked her curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 那张奇怪的照片引起了她的好奇。
senses.why: Curiosity is another response that is called forth rather than pushed in.
senses.whyCN: 好奇也是被唤出的回应，而不是被塞进去的。

senses.title: To stir an emotion
senses.definition: to bring a strong feeling such as fear, pity or laughter to the surface
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧、怜悯或笑意等强烈情绪浮到表面
senses.example: The empty street provoked a sense of unease.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道激起一种不安。
senses.why: Emotions are treated as things that can be summoned, which is the core of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被当作可以召唤的东西，这正是拉丁动词的核心。

senses.title: To draw criticism
senses.definition: to cause disapproval, complaint or public objection
senses.definitionCN: 引起不满、投诉或公开反对
senses.example: The decision provoked protests from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定招致居民的抗议。
senses.why: Criticism is a response with a negative charge, but the mechanism is still calling forth.
senses.whyCN: 批评是一种带负电的回应，但机制仍是「唤出」。

senses.title: To trigger an attack or symptom
senses.definition: to set off a physical episode such as a cough, a fit or an allergic response
senses.definitionCN: 触发咳嗽、发作或过敏反应等身体事件
senses.example: Cold air provoked a coughing fit.
senses.exampleCN: 冷空气诱发了一阵咳嗽。
senses.why: Medicine uses the verb for anything that sets a latent condition going.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个动词指任何让潜伏状况启动的因素。

senses.title: To incite action
senses.definition: to urge a group towards collective action, often unrest
senses.definitionCN: 鼓动一群人采取集体行动，常指骚动
senses.example: leaflets provoked a march the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 传单煽动了第二天早上的游行。
senses.why: A crowd is called into motion, and the verb keeps the image of a call rather than a push.
senses.whyCN: 人群被唤起来行动，这个动词保留「召唤」而非「推动」的画面。

intro.en: Provoke comes from Latin provocare, to call forth or challenge, from pro-, forth, and vocare, to call, from vox, voice. English took it through French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 provocare「唤出、挑战」，由 pro-「向前」与 vocare「呼叫」构成，而 vocare 出自 vox「声音」；英语十四世纪经法语引入。

items.en: Vox meant voice, and it is the source of vocal, voice and the whole calling family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「声音」，是 vocal、voice 以及整个「呼叫」词族的来源。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon, and it built verbs such as invoke, evoke and revoke.
items.cn: 这个词意为呼叫、召唤，构成了 invoke、evoke、revoke 等动词。

items.en: The prefix meant forward or forth, so provocare pictured a call sent out towards someone.
items.cn: 前缀意为向前、向外，所以这个词的画面是把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.en: The verb meant to call forth, to challenge, and in law to appeal against a decision.
items.cn: 这个动词意为唤出、挑战，在法律中指对裁决提出上诉。

items.en: English adopted the verb through French; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语经法语采用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十四世纪」。

items.en: The sense of stirring anger became dominant later, while the neutral sense of causing a response survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 「激起怒气」后来越来越占主导，而「引起回应」的中性义在正式写作中仍存活。

note.en: The first group shares the call root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of causing and stirring.
note.cn: 第一组与「provoke」共享「呼叫」词根或只是形近；第二组是与「引起、激起」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of stirring someone or something up.
entries.definitionCN: 指激怒、挑起这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that stirs a reaction or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指挑衅的、引人反应的。

entries.definition: To call out a memory or feeling, with the prefix meaning out.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤出记忆或情感，前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: To call upon, as a law or a power, with the prefix meaning in.
entries.definitionCN: 指援引法律或力量，前缀意为「向内」。

entries.definition: To call back, hence to cancel a right or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤回，因而指撤销权利或规定。

entries.definition: The stock of words, from the same voice root.
entries.definitionCN: 指词汇总量，同出「声音」词根。

entries.definition: To annoy mildly, with less drama than provoke.
entries.definitionCN: 指轻度惹恼，戏剧性不如本词。

entries.definition: To set off an event or reaction, often mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发事件或反应，常带机械意味。

entries.definition: To wake a feeling or interest in someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤起情感或兴趣。

entries.definition: To urge people towards violent or unlawful action.
entries.definitionCN: 指煽动人们采取暴力或违法行动。

entries.definition: To draw out a response or information, usually without anger.
entries.definitionCN: 指引出回应或信息，通常不含怒气。

entries.definition: To bother someone mildly and repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 指反复轻度打扰某人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the voice root, its four sibling verbs, and the neutral and angry branches of meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「声音」词根、它的四个兄弟动词，以及中性义与激怒义两条分支。

normal.en: Vox is voice, so provoke is to send a call out and wait for an answer.
normal.cn: vox 是「声音」，所以这个词是发出一声召唤，等着回应。

normal.en: Invoke, evoke and revoke share the same calling root with different prefixes.
normal.cn: invoke、evoke、revoke 与它共享同一「呼叫」词根，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Provoke a debate is neutral; provoke a crowd is not.
normal.cn: 「引发辩论」是中性说法，「激怒人群」则不是。

normal.en: Provocation and provocative are the noun and adjective of the same action.
normal.cn: 它的名词与形容词形式分别表示「挑衅」与「挑衅的」。

normal.en: Cold air can provoke a cough, which shows how wide the neutral sense reaches.
normal.cn: 冷空气能诱发咳嗽，可见中性义覆盖面之广。

abstract.en: To provoke is to open a door and refuse to say what is behind it.
abstract.cn: 激怒，就是打开一扇门却不说门后有什么。

abstract.en: Every provocation is a question the other person is expected to answer badly.
abstract.cn: 每一次挑衅，都是一个预期对方会答坏的问题。

abstract.en: A response called forth is not the same as a response forced in, and that difference is the word.
abstract.cn: 被唤出的回应与被塞进去的回应不同，这个差别就是这个词本身。

examples.en: The cartoon provoked angry letters from both sides.
examples.cn: 这幅漫画招致双方愤怒的来信。

examples.en: Her question provoked a thoughtful silence.
examples.cn: 她的问题引来一阵沉思的沉默。

examples.en: Dust can provoke an asthma attack in sensitive people.
examples.cn: 粉尘可能诱发敏感人群的哮喘发作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普罗沃克」——长杆一伸，水面荡开圈圈波纹：引发、激怒

root: 拉丁语 vox「声音」→ vocare「呼叫」→ provocare「唤出、挑战」（pro-「向前」+ vocare）；英语十四世纪经法语引入。与 evoke、invoke、revoke 同根不同前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all call something forth: anger, a challenge, a reaction, curiosity, emotion, criticism, a symptom and collective action.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把某物唤出：怒气、挑战、反应、好奇、情绪、批评、症状与集体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pole touches still water and rings spread outward from the point of contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：长杆触到静水，圈圈波纹从触点向外荡开。

branches.en: THE INVITATION TO ANGER: someone is deliberately stirred and expected to react.
branches.cn: 向怒气发出邀请：某人被有意激起，并被期待作出反应。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ANSWER: a report or a decision draws discussion, criticism or protest.
branches.cn: 公众的回应：报告或决定引出讨论、批评或抗议。

branches.en: THE SPARK OF CURIOSITY: interest appears because something strange is placed in view.
branches.cn: 好奇的火星：奇怪之物被摆在眼前，兴趣随之出现。

branches.en: THE SURFACING FEELING: fear, pity or laughter is brought up from below.
branches.cn: 浮上来的情绪：恐惧、怜悯或笑意从底下被带上来。

branches.en: THE LATENT EPISODE: a symptom starts, or a crowd is moved into action.
branches.cn: 潜伏的发作：症状启动，或人群被鼓动起来。

intro.en: Provoke is a Latin verb of calling, and the prefix is the piece that decides which way the call goes.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词，前缀决定这声呼唤朝哪个方向去。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vox, vocare and provocare; the pieces are well recorded, so no part of the word is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vox、vocare、provocare；这些部件有清楚记录，这个词没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole calling family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个「呼叫」词族的源头。

items.example: It built invoke, evoke and revoke.
It sends the call out towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.example: The verb carried both the neutral and the combative shades.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼有中性义与好斗色彩。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅；激怒；诱因」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「气人的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「挑衅地」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅者」（少用）

definition_zh: 心理的；心理学的；心理层面的；（小说）心理描写的；（优势、战争）心理上的；心理上合适的
definition_en: relating to the mind, to the study of the mind, or to effects that work through feelings rather than physical force
core_image: 打开一个人的头盖，里面不是齿轮而是流动的情绪与念头
scene: 长期睡眠不足会带来心理上的负担。The study found that long periods of noise produced measurable psychological stress even when hearing was unaffected.
sceneCN: 这里 psychological 是「心理层面的」（第 3 个义项：作用于情绪与精神，而非听觉器官）；句意：研究发现在长时间噪声下，即使听力未受影响，也会产生可测量的心理压力。图中可辨识物件：分贝计、被噪声包围的人形轮廓、下沉的情绪曲线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 心理的；心理学的；心理层面的；心理描写的

derivatives.zh: 心理学；心理
心理学家
心理上地
心理（口语）；心理学（口语）

senses.title: Belonging to the mind
senses.definition: relating to the mind and its processes of thought, feeling and perception
senses.definitionCN: 与心智及其思维、情感与知觉过程相关
senses.example: Sleep loss has both physical and psychological consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足既有生理后果，也有心理后果。
senses.why: Psyche meant 'breath, soul, mind'. Psychological marks whatever belongs to that inner life rather than to the body's machinery.
senses.whyCN: psychē 意为“气息、灵魂、心智”。psychological 标记属于这种内在生活、而非身体机制的东西。

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.definition: belonging to psychology as an academic or clinical field
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学术或临床领域的心理学
senses.example: The paper appeared in a leading psychological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份顶尖心理学期刊上。
senses.why: Once psychology became a laboratory science in the 19th century, psychological came to mean 'of the discipline', covering experiments, journals and clinics.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪心理学成为实验室科学之后，psychological 开始指“属于该学科的”，涵盖实验、期刊与诊所。

senses.title: Working through feeling
senses.definition: affecting a person through emotions and mental state rather than physical force
senses.definitionCN: 通过情绪与心理状态而非物理力量影响人
senses.example: The threat of redundancy caused psychological harm long before any job was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员的威胁在任何岗位真正消失之前就已造成心理伤害。
senses.why: The word names effects that travel through the mind: fear, shame or anxiety can do damage even when no physical injury occurs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名经由心智传导的影响：恐惧、羞耻或焦虑即使没有身体伤害，也能造成损伤。

senses.title: Based on mental measurement
senses.definition: measured or assessed through mental tests and reported feelings rather than physical instruments
senses.definitionCN: 通过心理测试与自述感受而非物理仪器来测量或评估
senses.example: The trial used psychological scales to rate anxiety before and after treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 试验用心理量表评定治疗前后的焦虑程度。
senses.why: Research needed a word for data that comes from questionnaires and scales, so psychological marks the measuring method as well as the subject.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要为来自问卷与量表的数据找个词，于是 psychological 既标记研究对象，也标记测量方法。

senses.title: An edge in the mind
senses.definition: giving an advantage by affecting confidence, fear or motivation rather than resources
senses.definitionCN: 通过影响信心、恐惧或动机而非资源来取得优势
senses.example: Winning the first set gave the team a psychological advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 赢下第一盘给这支队伍带来了心理优势。
senses.why: Competition uses the adjective for edges that exist only in the mind: the score is level, but one side already feels beaten or emboldened.
senses.whyCN: 竞争用这个形容词指只存在于心里的优势：比分持平，但一方已感到被击败或受到鼓舞。

senses.title: Written from the inside
senses.definition: of a novel or film: focused on inner motives and feelings rather than external action
senses.definitionCN: 指小说或电影聚焦内心动机与感受，而非外部动作
senses.example: Critics praised the novel as a psychological study of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说是对悲伤的心理研究。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the term for works that stay inside a character's mind, where plot matters less than motive.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借这个词指留在人物内心的作品，在这类作品中情节不如动机重要。

senses.title: The right moment for the mind
senses.definition: of a moment: judged to be the point when people are most ready to accept something
senses.definitionCN: 指被人判断为最易接受某事的时刻
senses.example: He waited for the psychological moment to raise the question of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 他等待心理上最合适的时机提出经费问题。
senses.why: The fixed phrase 'the psychological moment' treats timing as a mental condition: the instant when resistance is lowest and attention highest.
senses.whyCN: 固定说法“心理上的时机”把时机当作一种心理状态：阻力最低、注意最高的那一刻。

senses.title: Fought through the mind
senses.definition: of warfare or tactics: aimed at beliefs, morale and fear instead of physical targets
senses.definitionCN: 指针对信念、士气与恐惧而非物理目标的战争或战术
senses.example: Leaflets and broadcasts were part of a psychological campaign against the garrison.
senses.exampleCN: 传单与广播构成了针对守军的心理战的一部分。
senses.why: Military language uses the adjective when the target is morale: nothing is destroyed, yet the will to fight is attacked directly.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言在目标是士气时用这个形容词：没有东西被摧毁，但战斗意志被直接攻击。

intro.en: Psychological joins Greek psychē, 'breath, soul, mind', with logos, 'word, account, reason', through the Latin-formed psychologia. The -ical ending comes from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos. The word began as a label for the study of the soul and ended up covering stress, novels, morale and warfare.
intro.cn: psychological 把希腊语 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”与 logos“言说、道理、理性”结合，经由拉丁形式的 psychologia 而来。-ical 词尾来自拉丁 -icalis 与希腊 -ikos。这个词最初是“研究灵魂”的标签，后来覆盖压力、小说、士气与战争。

items.en: Psyche meant 'breath, life, soul'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with the idea of breathing, though no root is proved.
items.cn: psychē 意为“气息、生命、灵魂”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与“呼吸”的观念有关，但没有被证实的词根。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'. Combined with other stems, -logia named a field of study or a body of discourse.
items.cn: logos 意为“言说、记述、理性”。与其他词干结合时，-logia 命名一个研究领域或一套论述。

items.en: The compound psychologia was coined in Latin by 16th-century scholars for the study of the soul, before any laboratory existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 由 16 世纪学者在拉丁语中造出，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验室。

items.en: English formed psychological from psychology with the adjective suffix -ical, at first meaning 'of the soul or mind'.
items.cn: 英语用形容词后缀 -ical 从 psychology 造出 psychological，最初意为“属于灵魂或心智的”。

items.en: Wundt and others turned psychology into an experimental discipline, and psychological came to cover measurement, tests and clinical practice.
items.cn: 冯特等人把心理学变成实验学科，psychological 随之覆盖测量、测验与临床实践。

items.en: Psychological warfare was named in the two world wars, psychological novels flourished earlier in the century, and the adjective spread to stress, advantage and timing.
items.cn: 心理战在两次世界大战中得名，心理小说在 20 世纪初兴盛，这个形容词又扩散到压力、优势与时机。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from psychology, the adverb and the different-root physiological. The meaning group contrasts mental, emotional and cognitive descriptions.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与 psychology、副词，以及词根不同的 physiological；词义组比较 mental、emotional 与 cognitive 三类描述。

entries.definition: the study of the mind, or a person's mental make-up. It names the field, while psychological describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 对心智的研究，或某人的心理构成。它命名字科，而 psychological 描述属于该学科的东西。

entries.definition: in mental terms. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something affects the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 在心理层面上。它把形容词转为关于如何影响心智的陈述。

entries.definition: relating to the body's functions. It looks parallel but comes from physis 'nature' plus logos, a different stem from psyche.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体功能相关的。它看起来结构平行，却来自 physis“自然”加 logos，词干与 psychē 不同。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It comes from iatreia 'healing', not from logos 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗相关的。它来自 iatreia“治疗”，而非 logos“研究”。

entries.definition: relating to the mind. It is the plain everyday word and often pairs with health and illness, while psychological is more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智相关的。它是平实的日常词，常与健康、疾病搭配，而 psychological 更技术化。

entries.definition: relating to feelings. It covers one part of mental life, while psychological covers the whole inner system.
entries.definitionCN: 与情感相关的。它覆盖心理生活的一部分，而 psychological 覆盖整个内在系统。

entries.definition: relating to thinking, memory and perception. It names the intellectual side rather than feeling or morale.
entries.definitionCN: 与思维、记忆和知觉相关的。它指理智的一面，而非情绪或士气。

entries.definition: existing in a person's own experience. It marks the private side of what psychological studies measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于个人自身经验中的。它标记心理研究所测之物的私人一面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into psyche and logos, then let the inner-life picture cover stress, science, novels, advantage, timing and warfare.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 psyche 与 logos，再用内在生活的画面覆盖压力、科学、小说、优势、时机与战争。

normal.en: Split it as psyche + log + ical: mind + study + adjective. Psychological means 'of the study of the mind'.
normal.cn: 拆成 psyche + log + ical：心智、研究、形容词。psychological 意为“关于心智研究的”。

normal.en: Picture a head opened like a room, with feelings drifting around instead of gears.
normal.cn: 想象一个像房间一样打开的头，里面飘着情绪而不是齿轮。

normal.en: Physical harm hits the body; psychological harm hits the same person through fear and shame.
normal.cn: 物理伤害打身体；心理伤害通过恐惧与羞耻打同一个人。

normal.en: A psychological novel stays inside that room, watching motives instead of events.
normal.cn: 心理小说留在那个房间里，看动机而不是看事件。

normal.en: Psychological warfare attacks morale, so the target is that room rather than any building.
normal.cn: 心理战攻击士气，因此目标就是那个房间，而不是任何建筑。

abstract.en: Keep the two Greek halves visible: psyche is the subject, logos is the way of studying it.
abstract.cn: 让两个希腊部分保持可见：psychē 是对象，logos 是研究方式。

abstract.en: Notice that the adjective can describe both a science and a trick: the same word covers journals and warfare.
abstract.cn: 注意这个形容词既能描述科学也能描述手段：同一个词覆盖期刊与战争。

abstract.en: Contrast it with physiological: one studies the mind, the other the body, even though the words look like twins.
abstract.cn: 与 physiological 对照：一个研究心智，一个研究身体，尽管两词看起来像双胞胎。

examples.en: Researchers measured the psychological effects of isolation on long voyages.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了长期航行中隔离对心理的影响。

examples.en: The coach said the early goal gave his players a psychological lift.
examples.cn: 教练说那个早早的进球让球员们在心理上受到鼓舞。

examples.en: The museum mounted a psychological warfare exhibition from the cold war.
examples.cn: 博物馆举办了一场冷战心理战展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“赛可乐鸡扣”：赛场上喝口可乐，鸡血一扣，心理状态立刻不同。

root: 希腊 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”加 logos“言说、研究”构成 psychologia，加 -ical 为形容词；核心是“属于心智及其研究”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses point to the inner life: a mind that suffers, a science that studies it, an effect that travels through feeling, a scale that measures it, an advantage that lives in confidence, a novel that stays inside it, a moment when it is ready, and a war that attacks it directly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向内在生活：会受苦的心智、研究它的科学、经由情绪传导的影响、测量它的量表、存在于信心中的优势、留在它内部的小说、它准备好的时刻，以及直接攻击它的战争。

core.en: The inner life of a person, and everything that acts on it or measures it.
core.cn: 一个人的内在生活，以及作用于它或测量它的一切。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the mind itself and the discipline that studies it.
branches.cn: 对象：心智本身以及研究它的学科。

branches.en: EFFECT: harm or advantage arrives through feeling, not force.
branches.cn: 影响：伤害或优势经由情绪而非力量到来。

branches.en: MEASURE: scales and tests turn inner states into data.
branches.cn: 测量：量表与测验把内在状态变成数据。

branches.en: FICTION: a narrative stays inside motive rather than action.
branches.cn: 虚构：叙事留在动机内部，而非外部动作。

branches.en: TIMING AND WAR: the mind is either ready to yield or actively attacked.
branches.cn: 时机与战争：心智要么准备好让步，要么正被主动攻击。

intro.en: Psychological is psyche plus logos plus the adjective suffix -ical. The items below follow the Greek stems into nouns, adverbs and neighbouring disciplines.
intro.cn: psychological 由 psyche、logos 与形容词后缀 -ical 构成。下列条目沿着这两个希腊词干走到名词、副词与邻近学科。

latinIntro.en: The Greek entries give the two stems. They explain why psychology, psychiatry and psychosomatic all begin with the same word for soul.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语条目给出两个词干，解释了为什么 psychology、psychiatry 与 psychosomatic 都以同一个表示“灵魂”的词开头。

items.exampleCN: 这项调查追踪心理康复情况。

items.meaning: a person who studies the mind

items.example: Psychiatry treated the trauma with therapy and drugs.
items.exampleCN: 精神病学用治疗与药物处理创伤。

items.meaning: of symptoms caused or worsened by mental factors
items.meaningCN: 心身的；由心理因素引起的
items.exampleCN: 这皮疹被判断为心身性的。

items.meaning: the soul or mind as a whole
items.example: The myth describes the trials of Psyche.
items.exampleCN: 这个神话描述了普绪克的试炼。

a field of study or discourse

definition_zh: 心理学家；心理学工作者：以科学方法研究心智与行为的人，也指从事心理咨询、心理测验或组织应用的执业者
definition_en: a person trained in the scientific study of the mind and behaviour, or one who applies that training in counselling, testing or organisations
core_image: 隔着单向玻璃的观察室里，一个人记录受试者按键前的停顿，纸上画满一格一格的时间刻度
scene: 隔着一面单向玻璃，研究者记录受试者按键前的停顿，把每一次犹豫都标在时间轴上。The clinic hired a psychologist to treat those pauses as data rather than noise.
sceneCN: 这里指受过训练、以观察与测量研究心智与行为的人（第 1 个义项：心理学家这一职业身份）；句意为诊所请了一位心理学家，把这些停顿当作数据而非噪声。

pos.zh: 心理学家；心理学研究者
心理师；心理咨询或心理治疗执业者

derivatives.zh: psycho-（心智） + -logy（学科）→ 研究心智与行为的学科
psychology + -ical（属于……的）→ 属于心理或心理学的
psychological + -ly（方式副词）→ 从心理层面

senses.title: A researcher of mind and behaviour
senses.titleCN: 研究心智与行为的研究者
senses.definition: a person who studies mental processes and behaviour by experiment, observation or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 以实验、观察或测量研究心理过程与行为的人
senses.example: The psychologist ran the memory task with two hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位心理学家让两百名志愿者做了记忆任务。
senses.why: psychologist is psychology plus -ist 'one who practises', so the word names the person before it names any particular job.
senses.whyCN: psychologist 是 psychology 加表示「从事者」的 -ist，因此这个词先指人，再指具体岗位。

senses.title: A clinical or counselling practitioner
senses.definition: a licensed professional who assesses and treats emotional or behavioural difficulties through talk-based methods
senses.definitionCN: 以谈话等方法评估并处理情绪或行为困难的持照专业人员
senses.example: A clinical psychologist saw him weekly for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一位临床心理师每周为他看诊，持续了一年。
senses.why: the same training was applied to illness, so the title expanded from the laboratory to the consulting room.
senses.whyCN: 同样的训练被用于疾病，头衔便从实验室扩展到诊室。

senses.title: A school psychologist
senses.definition: a professional employed by a school to assess learning difficulties and support pupils and teachers
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于学校，评估学习困难并支持学生与教师的专业人员
senses.example: The school psychologist tested the pupil for a reading difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 学校心理师为这名学生做了阅读困难评估。
senses.why: schools need measurement and advice on learning, which is a natural home for the applied title.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要测量与学习建议，这正是这个应用头衔的自然落点。

senses.title: An educational psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies how people learn and advises on teaching, curriculum and assessment
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习，并就教学、课程与评估提供建议的专家
senses.example: An educational psychologist redesigned the spelling programme.
senses.exampleCN: 一位教育心理学家重新设计了拼写课程。
senses.why: the discipline has a branch for learning, and its practitioner carries the branch name.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科有专门研究学习的分支，从业者便带着该分支的名字。

senses.title: An industrial and organisational psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who applies psychology to hiring, teamwork, performance and workplace well-being
senses.definitionCN: 把心理学用于招聘、团队、绩效与职场福祉的专家
senses.example: An industrial psychologist audited the hiring tests for bias.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工业心理学家审查了招聘测试中的偏见。
senses.why: wherever people work in groups, measurement and behaviour study can be sold as a service, and the title follows the market.
senses.whyCN: 只要人们成群工作，测量与行为研究就能作为服务出售，头衔便跟着市场走。

senses.title: A tester who administers assessments
senses.titleCN: 实施与解释心理测评的人
senses.definition: a person who administers standardised tests and interprets the scores for schools, clinics or courts
senses.definitionCN: 为学校、诊所或法庭实施标准化测验并解释分数的人
senses.example: The psychologist administered the standardised test under timed conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 心理师在计时条件下实施了标准化测验。
senses.why: testing is the oldest applied skill of the field, and the person who administers a test is still called by the same title.
senses.whyCN: 测评是这一领域最古老的应用技能，实施测验的人仍用同一头衔。

senses.title: A sport psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who works with athletes on attention, arousal, routine and competitive stress
senses.definitionCN: 帮助运动员处理注意、唤醒水平、赛前程序与竞赛压力的专家
senses.example: The sport psychologist taught the sprinter a pre-race routine.
senses.exampleCN: 运动心理师教给短跑选手一套赛前程序。
senses.why: performance under pressure is a measurable behaviour, so a branch of practice grew around it.
senses.whyCN: 压力下的表现是一种可测量的行为，围绕它便长出一个实践分支。

senses.title: A forensic or legal psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who assesses memory, risk or competence for courts and legal proceedings
senses.definitionCN: 为法庭与法律程序评估记忆、风险或行为能力的人
senses.example: A forensic psychologist warned the court about false eyewitness confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 一位司法心理师提醒法庭注意目击者的虚假自信。
senses.why: courts need evidence about perception and decision, which puts the title inside the courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要关于知觉与决策的证据，这个头衔因此进了审判庭。

senses.title: The older student of the soul
senses.definition: a scholar of the soul or mind in the period before psychology became an experimental science
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学成为实验科学之前研究灵魂或心智的学者
senses.example: Eighteenth-century psychologists argued about the seat of the soul.
senses.exampleCN: 十八世纪的心理学家争论灵魂的居所。
senses.why: the Greek root psykhe meant 'breath, life, soul', so the earliest bearer of the title studied the soul, not behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 psykhe 意为「气息、生命、灵魂」，最早带这个头衔的人研究的是灵魂，而非行为。

intro.en: Psychologist is psychology plus the agent suffix -ist. Psychology is a New Latin coinage joining Greek psykhe 'breath, life, soul' and logos 'word, account, reason'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: psychologist 是 psychology 加表施动者的后缀 -ist。psychology 是新拉丁语造词，把希腊语 psykhe「气息、生命、灵魂」与 logos「言说、论述、理性」合在一起。年代为约数。

items.en: Psykhe meant 'breath, life, soul', the breath that marks a living being; the related verb psychein meant 'to breathe'. The word could also name the departed spirit.
items.cn: psykhe 意为「气息、生命、灵魂」，是标记活物的那口气；相关动词 psychein 意为「呼吸」。这个词也可指离体的亡灵。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. In compound names of disciplines, -logia meant 'the study or systematic account of'.
items.cn: logos 意为「言词、叙述、道理、理性」。在学科复合名称中，-logia 意为「对……的研究或系统论述」。

items.en: The compound psychologia appeared in sixteenth-century academic Latin for the study of the soul, before any experimental method existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 在 16 世纪的学术拉丁语中出现，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验方法。

items.en: Psychology entered English in the seventeenth century as the study of the soul; the modern scientific sense dates from the nineteenth century, when laboratories and measurement were established.
items.cn: psychology 在 17 世纪进入英语，指对灵魂的研究；现代科学义始于 19 世纪，那时实验室与测量方法已经建立。

items.en: Greek -istes 'one who practises' passed through Latin -ista into English -ist, so psychologist names the person who practises psychology.
items.cn: 希腊语 -istes「从事者」经拉丁语 -ista 进入英语成为 -ist，因此 psychologist 指从事心理学的人。

items.en: Source uncertain (first coiner and first English use): several sixteenth-century authors used psychologia independently, and the exact first English use of psychologist is not settled; the date given here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首创者与英语首见）：16 世纪有数位作者各自使用 psychologia，psychologist 的确切英语首见亦无定论；此处年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds titles built on the same psych- stem that name different roles; group two holds people who also sit with a client but are trained differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 psych- 词干、却指不同角色的头衔；第二组是同样与来访者对坐、但训练路径不同的人。

entries.definition: A physician who has completed medical training and may prescribe drugs; a psychologist normally cannot prescribe.
entries.definitionCN: 完成医学训练的医生，可以开药；心理学家通常不能开药。

entries.definition: A practitioner trained in the Freudian or related analytic tradition, not in academic psychology as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 受弗洛伊德或相关分析传统训练的人，而非接受整个学术心理学训练的人。

entries.definition: A specialist in the construction and statistical validation of tests; the role is narrower than the general title.
entries.definitionCN: 专做测验编制与统计验证的人，角色比通称更窄。

entries.definition: A general title for one who treats mental or physical difficulties; many therapists lack a psychology degree.
entries.definitionCN: 处理心理或身体困难者的通称；许多治疗师并没有心理学学位。

entries.definition: A practitioner who offers structured listening and advice, often in schools or community services.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有结构的倾听与建议的从业者，常见于学校或社区服务。

entries.definition: Anyone who works directly with patients, including physicians and nurses; the word marks setting, not discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 任何直接接触病人的人，包括医生与护士；这个词标记工作场所，不标记学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: psykhe 'soul' plus logos 'account': an account of the soul, later an account of behaviour.
normal.cn: psykhe「灵魂」加 logos「论述」：关于灵魂的论述，后来变成关于行为的论述。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, so psychologist is the one who practises what psychology studies.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人，因此 psychologist 就是从事心理学所研究之事的人。

normal.en: The family runs psychology, psychological, psychologically, psychologize, psychologism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 psychology、psychological、psychologically、psychologize、psychologism。

normal.en: Job titles pin the branches: clinical, school, educational, industrial, sport and forensic.
normal.cn: 岗位头衔钉住各分支：临床、学校、教育、工业、运动与司法。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the soul, which is why the spelling begins with psych- and not with behav-.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是灵魂，这正是拼写以 psych- 开头而不是以 behav- 开头的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a person who watches a key press and writes down a number instead of a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人盯着一次按键，写下的是一个数字，而不是一种感受。

abstract.en: Picture two rooms separated by glass: one person performs, the other measures.
abstract.cn: 想象被玻璃隔开的两间屋子：一间里的人在表现，另一间的人在测量。

abstract.en: Picture an old manuscript titled 'on the soul' slowly acquiring a stopwatch.
abstract.cn: 想象一册题为「论灵魂」的旧手稿，慢慢多了一只秒表。

examples.en: The psychologist compared reaction times across age groups.
examples.cn: 这位心理学家比较了不同年龄组的反应时。

examples.en: A psychologist may not prescribe drugs unless trained as a physician.
examples.cn: 心理学家除非受过医学训练，否则不能开药。

examples.en: The school hired a psychologist to review its assessment policy.
examples.cn: 学校聘请了一位心理师来审查评估政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: psycho（心智）+ log（研究）+ ist（人）＝ 研究心智的人；记「玻璃两侧：一侧表现，一侧测量」。

root: 希腊 psykhe「气息、生命、灵魂」+ logos「言说、论述、理性」，经新拉丁 psychologia「灵魂之学」加 -istes「从事者」；更深词源无定论，psykhe 与「呼吸」的联系为通行解释。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one trained observer: first the researcher, then the clinic, the school, the classroom, the office, the test room, the track, the court, and finally the older student of the soul.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一个受过训练的观察者展开：先是研究者，再依次是诊室、学校、课堂、办公室、测评室、赛场、法庭，最后回到早期研究灵魂的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained observer on one side of glass, recording a measurable act on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：受过训练的观察者站在玻璃一侧，记录另一侧可测量的行为。

branches.en: THE RESEARCHER: the title begins as the person who studies and measures mind and behaviour.
branches.cn: 研究者：这个头衔最初指研究并测量心智与行为的人。

branches.en: THE HELPING ROOMS: clinic and school take the same training into assessment and care.
branches.cn: 助人的房间：诊室与学校把同一套训练带进评估与照护。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONS: learning and work each grow a branch with its own title.
branches.cn: 机构：学习与工作各自长出一个带专属头衔的分支。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE TRACK: administering a score and shaping a routine are both applied measurement.
branches.cn: 测评与赛场：给分与塑造赛前程序，都是应用性的测量。

branches.en: THE COURT AND THE SOUL: the title reaches legal evidence at one end and the old study of the soul at the other.
branches.cn: 法庭与灵魂：这个头衔一端抵达法律证据，另一端回到古老的灵魂之学。

intro.en: Psychologist can be read as two Greek roots plus two suffixes: psykhe and logos build the discipline, -logia names it, and -ist names the person.
intro.cn: psychologist 可以读作两个希腊词根加两个后缀：psykhe 与 logos 构成学科，-logia 命名学科，-ist 命名人。

latinIntro.en: The discipline name is New Latin, coined from Greek elements; Latin supplies the shape of the suffixes -logia and -ista, which English shortened to -logy and -ist.
latinIntro.cn: 学科名是新拉丁语，用希腊成分造出；拉丁语提供了 -logia 与 -ista 后缀的外形，英语将其缩短为 -logy 与 -ist。

senses.title: The science of the mind

senses.definition: the scientific study of the mind and behavior
senses.definitionCN: 对心理与行为的科学研究
